name: SPX JEV questions, both lanes

generated_from.set: SPX JEV question set, final (round 3: audits applied)

status: generated by spec/write_question_docs.py: edit the set and regenerate, never this file
owner_rule: A question goes to shadow only once proven not to help JEV's direction call; unproven questions stay live and the learning loop's weights sort them out.
how_to_use: Step 2 of the pipeline. Each lane asks the questions whose lanes name it (the live lane thirty_minute, the opening lane opening_five_minute), at the reads its schedule names: live ones count in the sums, shadow ones are asked and logged but never summed, dark ones are never asked. A question with sleep_when is asked only when its label family says it is awake. Every threshold is a name in braces filled from spx_jev/cuts.py.

groups.purpose: Feed the 09:35-10:30 ten-minute five-way call: gap size, which side of the settled open wins, fresh session extremes, how contested and busy the open is, and how choppy or one-way its path has been.

gap_size.cadence: once at the 09:35 read on the settled open; answer held as a day constant to 10:30 (code weights it by minutes since the open)
gap_size.ask: How large was this morning's gap from yesterday's close?
gap_size.instructions: Read `gap.size`. How large was this morning's gap between yesterday's close and the settled open, whichever way it went, against the recent sessions' gaps?
criteria: the gap was in the bottom third of the recent sessions' gaps
the gap was in the middle third of the recent sessions' gaps
the gap was in the top third of the recent sessions' gaps
code_criteria: |gap| larger than under a third of the prior sessions' |gap| (bottom third)
|gap| larger than a third to two thirds of them (middle third)
|gap| larger than over two thirds of them (top third)
gap_size.why: Gap size sets how busy the first half hour is; it says nothing about the next 10 minutes' direction, so it serves size only and is asked once instead of twelve identical times.

opening_side.cadence: every 5 min 09:45-10:30, from the first read with a live tape unit (code weights by minutes-since-open bucket; the 09:50-10:05 bucket carries the effect)
opening_side.ask: Which side of the settled open does the opening favour now?
opening_side.instructions: Read `open.path`. Where price is now, in tape units from the settled open, decides first. Check rotating first. Which side of the settled open does the opening favour now?

criteria.up_firm: now more than one tape unit above the open, and it has given back less than the stall line of its high
criteria.up_fading: now more than one tape unit above the open, but it has given back the stall line or more of its high
criteria.rotating: within one tape unit of the open now
criteria.down_fading: now more than one tape unit below the open, but it has given back the stall line or more of its low
criteria.down_firm: now more than one tape unit below the open, and it has given back less than the stall line of its low

code_criteria.down_fading: mirror of up_fading below the open
code_criteria.down_firm: mirror of up_firm below the open

opening_side.why: Replaces opening_drive's seven options with five signed ones: stalling and failed flipped sign between windows on 10-24 reads, and tested_then_reversed fired on 2 of 59 days.

fresh_extreme_5m.cadence: every 5 min 09:45-10:30 with a 5-minute window; then every 30-minute read with a 30-minute window
fresh_extreme_5m.ask: Did price just set a new session high or low, or stall near one?
fresh_extreme_5m.instructions: Read `open.fresh_extreme` and `price.day_range_position`. Over the window the label names, did price set a new high or low for the session, or is it sitting near one without setting a new one? Check in order: both_new, new_high, new_low, stalled_near_high, stalled_near_low, middle.

criteria.new_high: price set a new session high in the window and no new low
criteria.new_low: price set a new session low in the window and no new high
criteria.both_new: price set both a new high and a new low in the window
criteria.stalled_near_high: no new extreme in the window, and price sits in the top band of today's range
criteria.stalled_near_low: no new extreme in the window, and price sits in the bottom band of today's range
criteria.middle: no new extreme, and price sits between the top and bottom bands of today's range

code_criteria.new_high: max high of the window's bars > session high before them; no new low

fresh_extreme_5m.why: The one opening state with positive held-out skill on the lane's own grading; it folds the opening-range break in as a label clause because the break carries almost nothing once the fresh extreme is known.

open_contested.ask: How contested has the settled open been so far?
open_contested.instructions: Read `open.settled_open_crosses`. How contested has the settled open been so far, against the same minute on the recent sessions?

criteria.one_sided: price's count of crossings of the settled open so far ranks in the bottom third of the recent sessions' counts to this minute (a tie is not beaten)
criteria.some_crossing: price's count of crossings of the settled open so far ranks in the middle third of the recent sessions' counts to this minute (a tie is not beaten)
criteria.contested: price's count of crossings of the settled open so far ranks in the top third of the recent sessions' counts to this minute (a tie is not beaten)

code_criteria.one_sided: crosses beat under {third_lo} of the last {night_rank_count} sessions' crosses to this minute (bottom third; a tie is not beaten)
code_criteria.some_crossing: crosses beat {third_lo} to {third_hi} of them (middle third)
code_criteria.contested: crosses beat over {third_hi} of them (top third)

open_contested.why: Repeated fights over the settled open mean two-way flow is active: the next 10 minutes run larger, even after a quiet 5 minutes, which moves weight out of the five-way flat bucket. Crossings pile up with the minutes since the open, so the count is judged against the same minute on the recent sessions, not a fixed count. Asked from 09:45, when ten minutes of path exist (open.chop and the tape unit go live then): at 09:40 five bars give 0 to 2 crossings and 2 already ranks top third. Crossings are small whole numbers and a tie is not beaten, so the thirds come out uneven (about 42/25/32% bottom/middle/top over 09:40-10:30 on 39 replayed days).

opening_pace.cadence: every 5 min 09:45-10:30 (asleep while the tape unit is held before 09:45)
opening_pace.ask: How busy is the opening for this time of day?
opening_pace.instructions: Read `tape.unit_vs_normal` and `range.today_vs_normal`. Check very_busy first. How busy is the opening right now for this time of day?
criteria: the tape unit and today's range both in the bottom third for this time of day, or one in the bottom third and the other in the middle third
both in the middle third for this time of day, or one in the top third and the other in the bottom third
one in the top third for this time of day and the other in the middle third
both in the top third for this time of day, or the tape unit wider than all of the recent sessions
code_criteria: both bottom third, or one bottom one middle
both middle, or one top one bottom
one top third, one middle
both top third, or the wider-than-all flag
opening_pace.why: The median of three 5-minute ranges is the lane's own outcome unit and forecasts the next 10 minutes better than the last 5 minutes, which also carries the stale 09:30 catch-up.

opening_chop.ask: How choppy or one-way has the open been since the settled open?
opening_chop.instructions: Read `open.chop`. Since the settled open, has price's path been choppy, mixed or one-way, against the same minute on the recent sessions?

criteria.choppy: the path since the settled open is in the bottom third of the recent sessions' paths to this minute for how one-way it was: price travelled far for little net move
criteria.mixed: the path is in the middle third of the recent sessions' paths to this minute
criteria.one_way: the path is in the top third of the recent sessions' paths to this minute: most of the distance travelled went one way

code_criteria.choppy: path efficiency beats under {third_lo} of the last {night_rank_count} sessions' at this minute (bottom third; a tie is not beaten)

opening_chop.why: Owner decision #10 (2026-09-27): whether the open has been chopping around the settled open or travelling one way is a regime read the five-way call lacks; open_contested counts the fights over one level, this measures the whole path. Path efficiency falls with the minutes since the open, so it is judged against the same minute on the recent sessions, not a fixed line.

groups.purpose: The non-price opening reads: net volume, TICK (average and bursts), large 0DTE prints and premium bursts, the call-put swing of new 0DTE volume, the same-day put tilt against the clock, and chips/financials tells.

open_net_volume_lean.ask: Since the open, has net volume leaned to buying or selling against a usual morning?
open_net_volume_lean.instructions: Read `breadth.open_net_volume`. Since the open, compared with the same minute on recent sessions, has net volume leaned to buying, to selling, or split between NYSE-wide and S&P 500 stocks? Each total's third decides: the top third leans to buying, the bottom third to selling, the middle third is no lean.

criteria.both_buying: NYSE and S&P 500 net volume since the open both rank in the top third of the same total at this minute on recent sessions
criteria.both_selling: both rank in the bottom third
criteria.split: one ranks in the top or bottom third and the other does not rank in the same third
criteria.no_lean: both rank in the middle third

code_criteria.both_buying: rank(VOLD) and rank(VOLSPD) both higher than more than {third_hi} of the prior sessions at this minute (top third)
code_criteria.both_selling: both higher than fewer than {third_lo} of them (bottom third)
code_criteria.split: exactly one in an outer third, or one in the top third and the other in the bottom third

open_net_volume_lean.why: The only opening input in review whose interval clears zero and holds after removing the price move; it is the 10-minute breadth read round 1 asked for, with the advance-decline thrust folded in. Each total is ranked against the same minute on recent sessions (owner rule 2026-09-27), no longer sized in usual swings against a fixed line.

opening_tick_lean.ask: Since the open, how one-sided has market-wide buying and selling been?
opening_tick_lean.instructions: Read `breadth.opening_tick`. Since the open, how one-sided has market-wide buying and selling been? Check the one-sided options first, then a burst both ways, then the mean's third.

criteria.one_sided_buying: TICK highs reached the top burst band for these minutes {open_cluster_min} or more times and its lows never reached the bottom band
criteria.leaning_buying: not one-sided and no bursts both ways; TICK's mean since the open ranks in the top third of the same mean at this minute on recent sessions
criteria.two_way_open: not one-sided, and TICK burst both ways or its mean ranks in the middle third
criteria.leaning_selling: not one-sided and no bursts both ways; the mean ranks in the bottom third
criteria.one_sided_selling: TICK lows reached the bottom burst band {open_cluster_min} or more times and its highs never reached the top band

code_criteria.one_sided_buying: bursts >= {open_cluster_min} above the same-minute {tick_burst_pct} percentile of bar highs, none below the mirror (checked first)
code_criteria.leaning_buying: not one-sided, not both ways; mean since the open higher than more than {third_hi} of the prior sessions at this minute (top third)
code_criteria.two_way_open: not one-sided; bursts both ways, or mean in the middle third
code_criteria.leaning_selling: not one-sided, not both ways; mean higher than fewer than {third_lo} of them (bottom third)

opening_tick_lean.why: Traders read opening TICK clusters as trend-day tells; the fixed plus-or-minus-1000 line may never fire on SPX (probe closes -829..+944), so the burst band is a same-minute percentile of bar highs and lows.

big_print_lean_open.ask: Which way did the large same-day option trades of the last {window_10_min} minutes lean?
big_print_lean_open.instructions: Read `options.big_prints_10`. Over the last {window_10_min} minutes, did large single same-day option trades happen, and which way did their premium lean compared with the same minutes on recent sessions?

criteria.bullish_lean: at least {big_min_prints} large trades, and the share of their premium on calls bought or puts sold ranked in the top third of the same share at this minute on recent sessions
criteria.bearish_lean: at least {big_min_prints} large trades, and that share ranked in the bottom third
criteria.mixed: at least {big_min_prints} large trades, and that share ranked in the middle third, or the side of none of their premium could be told

code_criteria.bullish_lean: large trade = a single trade at or above the size the same-clock {big_print_pct} share of single trades in these minutes stayed at or under, pooled over up to the last {night_rank_count} sessions (at least {same_clock_min_sessions}); count >= {big_min_prints}; bullish premium share higher than more than {third_hi} of the same share on the prior sessions with {big_min_prints} or more large trades (top third)
code_criteria.bearish_lean: count >= {big_min_prints}; bullish premium share rank below {third_lo} (bottom third)
code_criteria.mixed: count >= {big_min_prints}; bullish premium share rank from {third_lo} to {third_hi} (middle third), or no side could be told

big_print_lean_open.why: An opening flow read of single large trades, not the whole tape, which is why the aggressor-lean shadow result does not settle it. Its contrarian sign was measured on the old 100-lot definition and is not yet measured on the ranked one.

zero_dte_side_shift_open.ask: Did new same-day option volume in the last {window_10_min} minutes shift to calls or to puts?
zero_dte_side_shift_open.instructions: Read `options.call_put_shift_10m`. Over the last {window_10_min} minutes, did new same-day option volume swing to calls or to puts against the day's split, compared with the same swing at this minute on recent sessions?

criteria.shift_to_calls: new volume not too thin, and its swing toward calls against the day's split ranked in the top third of the same swing at this minute on recent sessions
criteria.shift_to_puts: new volume not too thin, and the swing ranked in the bottom third, toward puts
criteria.no_shift: new volume not too thin, and the swing ranked in the middle third
criteria.too_thin: too little new volume to judge, whatever the swing

code_criteria.shift_to_calls: not too_thin; swing = call share last window - call share since open, higher than more than {third_hi} of the same swing at this minute on up to the last {night_rank_count} sessions, needing {same_clock_min_sessions} (top third)
code_criteria.shift_to_puts: not too_thin; swing rank below {third_lo} (bottom third)
code_criteria.no_shift: not too_thin; swing rank from {third_lo} to {third_hi} (middle third)
code_criteria.too_thin: new contracts higher than fewer than {thin_volume_pct} of the same 10 minutes' new contracts on the prior sessions

zero_dte_side_shift_open.why: 0DTE is about half of SPX option volume and the opening flow is where it shows first; the sign (hedging vs chasing) is unknown, so code learns it.

put_tilt_vs_clock.sleep_when: fewer than {same_clock_min_sessions} prior sessions with quotes at this minute, or a needed option price missing (label omitted)
put_tilt_vs_clock.ask: How steeply are same-day puts priced over calls against recent sessions at this minute?
put_tilt_vs_clock.instructions: Read `skew.put_tilt_vs_usual`. Compared with the same minute on recent sessions, how steeply are same-day puts priced over same-day calls right now? Check call_tilt first; then the verdict after the rank decides.

criteria.steep_put_tilt: a steep put tilt for this minute: puts priced over calls more steeply than on most recent sessions at this minute
criteria.usual_tilt: a usual tilt for this minute
criteria.flat_tilt: a flat tilt for this minute: puts priced over calls less steeply than on most recent sessions at this minute, but still at or above calls
criteria.call_tilt: same-day calls are priced above same-day puts at equal distance

code_criteria.steep_put_tilt: tilt rank >= {skew_steep_rank} vs the prior sessions at the same minute
code_criteria.flat_tilt: rank <= {skew_flat_rank} and put-call gap is zero or positive
code_criteria.call_tilt: put IV minus call IV at equal distance is negative (checked first)

put_tilt_vs_clock.why: Skew was not missing from history after all: the tape's quotes rebuild it. Raw skew is the clock (it decays from 0.15 to 0.03 through the day), so only the clock rank is asked; the far-put wing rides as a clause.

opening_tells_10m.ask: Did semiconductors or financials break away from the index in the last {window_10_min} minutes?
opening_tells_10m.instructions: Read `tells.sector_lead_10m`. Over the last {window_10_min} minutes, after scaling for how much each normally moves, did semiconductors or financials break away from the index, and which way?

criteria.both_up: semis and financials both ran ahead upward by a top-fifth margin for this time
criteria.both_down: both ran ahead downward by a top-fifth margin
criteria.financials_only: only financials broke away, either way (a rates tell)
criteria.split: one broke away up and the other down
criteria.in_line: neither broke away by a top-fifth margin

opening_tells_10m.why: Chips lead the AI-weighted index at the open; splitting the semis option by side lets the loop learn direction without the side hiding in the label.

opening_premium_burst.cadence: every 5 min 09:40-10:30, awake only when the last 5 minutes' 0DTE premium is in the top fifth for these minutes
opening_premium_burst.sleep_when: premium rank < {top_fifth}, or fewer than {same_clock_min_sessions} prior sessions with a whole lob-flow tape at this minute
opening_premium_burst.ask: Which way did the burst of same-day option premium lean?
opening_premium_burst.instructions: Read `options.premium_burst_5m`. A burst of same-day option premium just traded. Which way did its premium lean, compared with the same five minutes' lean on recent sessions?

criteria.burst_bullish: the share of the burst's premium on calls bought or puts sold ranked in the top third of the same five minutes' share on recent sessions
criteria.burst_bearish: that share ranked in the bottom third
criteria.burst_two_way: that share ranked in the middle third, or the side of none of its premium could be told

code_criteria.burst_bullish: premium rank >= {top_fifth}; bullish premium share higher than more than {third_hi} of the same five minutes' share on up to the last {night_rank_count} sessions, burst or not, needing {same_clock_min_sessions} (top third)
code_criteria.burst_bearish: premium rank >= {top_fifth}; bullish share rank below {third_lo} (bottom third)
code_criteria.burst_two_way: premium rank >= {top_fifth}; bullish share rank from {third_lo} to {third_hi} (middle third), or no side could be told

opening_premium_burst.why: A premium burst in the first hour is the tape's loudest opening flow read; round 1 cut it only to keep a request at six.

tick_extreme_follow.cadence: every 5 min 09:40-10:30, awake only when a TICK burst printed in the last 5 minutes
tick_extreme_follow.sleep_when: no TICK burst in the last 5 minutes
tick_extreme_follow.ask: Did SPX follow the NYSE TICK's burst to an extreme?
tick_extreme_follow.instructions: Read `breadth.tick_extreme_5m`. NYSE TICK just burst to an extreme for this minute. Did SPX follow it over the same five minutes with a real move (one outside the bottom third of the same five minutes on recent sessions) on the burst's side? Check both_ways first.

criteria.buy_burst_followed: a buying burst, and SPX rose with a real move: its five-minute move ranks outside the bottom third of the same five minutes on recent sessions
criteria.buy_burst_stalled: a buying burst, and SPX did not rise with a real move: it fell, or its move ranks in the bottom third
criteria.sell_burst_followed: a selling burst, and SPX fell with a real move
criteria.sell_burst_stalled: a selling burst, and SPX did not fall with a real move: it rose, or its move ranks in the bottom third
criteria.both_ways: bursts both ways in the same five minutes

code_criteria.both_ways: high above the {tick_burst_pct} band and low below the mirror band (checked first)
code_criteria.buy_burst_followed: high burst only, SPX five-minute move up, |move| higher than {third_lo} or more of the prior sessions' five-minute moves to this minute (not the bottom third)
code_criteria.buy_burst_stalled: high burst only, move down or in the bottom third

tick_extreme_follow.why: Round 1 named a five-minute TICK-extreme read as the opening lane's round-2 candidate; a burst the index does not follow is the classic absorption tell.

groups.purpose: Day constants asked once at the 09:35 read and held: the heavyweight gap split, the open against yesterday's range, VIX's first print against the gap, and the morning brief against the gap.

heavyweight_gap_split.cadence: once at the 09:35 read on the settled open; answer held as a day constant through the lane and the 30-minute reads to 11:32
heavyweight_gap_split.sleep_when: |largest single-name contribution| not in the top third of the last {night_rank_count} sessions' largest; fewer than {same_clock_min_sessions} prior sessions with yesterday's close, a settled open and every heavyweight's price
heavyweight_gap_split.ask: Did the rest of the index gap the same way as the heavyweight that moved it?
heavyweight_gap_split.instructions: Read `leaders.heavyweight_gap`. One of the largest index stocks moved the index by a top-third single-name contribution between yesterday's close and the settled open, against the recent sessions' largest. Did the rest of the index gap the same way, the other way, or barely move?
heavyweight_gap_split.dark_reason: the index weights of its largest stocks (state/spx_leaders/weights.json), which nothing writes yet

criteria.shock_up_rest_up: one heavyweight lifted the index by a top-third contribution and the rest of the index also gapped up, its gap above the bottom third of the recent sessions' rest-of-index gaps
criteria.shock_down_rest_down: one heavyweight dragged the index by a top-third contribution and the rest also gapped down, above the bottom third
criteria.shock_up_rest_down: one heavyweight lifted the index by a top-third contribution while the rest gapped down, above the bottom third
criteria.shock_down_rest_up: one heavyweight dragged the index by a top-third contribution while the rest gapped up, above the bottom third
criteria.shock_rest_flat: one heavyweight moved the index by a top-third contribution and the rest's gap was in the bottom third: it barely moved

code_criteria.shock_up_rest_up: |largest contribution| in the top third of the last {night_rank_count} sessions' largest (rank >= {third_hi}), up; |rest gap| above the bottom third of theirs (rank >= {third_lo}), up
code_criteria.shock_down_rest_down: contribution top third, down; rest gap above the bottom third, down
code_criteria.shock_up_rest_down: contribution top third, up; rest gap above the bottom third, down
code_criteria.shock_down_rest_up: contribution top third, down; rest gap above the bottom third, up
code_criteria.shock_rest_flat: contribution top third; |rest gap| in the bottom third (rank < {third_lo})

heavyweight_gap_split.why: When one stock is the index, SPX's gap is not the market's gap; on earnings reaction days the reporter's gap held and drifted instead of fading, which gap_origin used to mislabel as thin overnight drift.

open_vs_prior_range.cadence: once at the 09:35 read; answer held as a day constant through the lane and the 30-minute reads to 11:32
open_vs_prior_range.ask: Where did the open land against yesterday's high and low?
open_vs_prior_range.instructions: Read `levels.open_vs_prior_range`. Where is the open against yesterday's high and low?

criteria.above_prior_high: opened more than the buffer above yesterday's high
criteria.upper_inside: inside, or within the buffer of, yesterday's high: upper half of yesterday's range
criteria.lower_inside: inside, or within the buffer of, yesterday's low: lower half of yesterday's range
criteria.below_prior_low: opened more than the buffer below yesterday's low

code_criteria.upper_inside: open above the midpoint and <= prior high + {outside_buffer_sigma}
code_criteria.lower_inside: open below the midpoint and >= prior low - {outside_buffer_sigma}

open_vs_prior_range.why: An open outside yesterday's whole range meets no overhead or underfoot trade from the day before; it is a stronger vote than the gap alone and sets up a bigger morning.

vix_overnight_surprise.cadence: once at the 09:35 read; answer held as a day constant through the lane and the 30-minute reads to 11:32
vix_overnight_surprise.ask: Did VIX open higher, in line or lower than the overnight gap would leave it?
vix_overnight_surprise.instructions: Read `vol.vix_overnight_surprise`. Is VIX's first print today richer, in line, or cheaper than the overnight gap would normally leave it, against the same surprise on the recent sessions' openings? The label's third decides.

criteria.fear_rich: VIX opened richer against what the gap implies than on most recent sessions: the top third of their openings
criteria.in_line: the middle third of the recent sessions' openings
criteria.fear_cheap: VIX opened cheaper against what the gap implies than on most recent sessions: the bottom third of their openings

code_criteria.fear_rich: VIX open - implied, ranked with richer highest against the same on the prior sessions' openings: share of them it beats > {third_hi} (top third)

vix_overnight_surprise.why: Raw overnight VIX just repeats the gap (corr -0.79); what is new is hedging demand beyond the price move, and it leans contrarian.

brief_vs_tape.cadence: once at the 09:35 read; answer held as a day constant through the lane and the 30-minute reads to 11:32
brief_vs_tape.ask: What does the morning news brief add to this morning's gap?
brief_vs_tape.instructions: Read `news.morning_brief`. Check no_view first. Compared with this morning's gap, what does the morning news brief add?

criteria.no_view: the brief barely leans or has low confidence
criteria.restates: the brief leans the same way as a real gap, one larger than the bottom third of the recent days' gaps
criteria.leans_against: the brief leans the opposite way to a real gap
criteria.leans_without_move: the brief takes a side while the gap is in the bottom third of the recent days' gaps, no real gap

code_criteria.restates: same sign as a gap above the bottom third of the last {night_rank_count} days' gaps (gap_open.gap_rank)
code_criteria.leans_against: opposite sign, gap above the bottom third

brief_vs_tape.why: The brief is the only news read the station makes, but it mostly repeats the futures; asking what it adds keeps it from double-counting the gap. Only leans_against can add anything.

groups.purpose: The single carrier of the move's sign plus how the move was made: with or against the day, burst/choppy/clean, one-way hours, wide chop under a flat net move, and the day's character.

price_move_5way.ask: Over the last {window_30_min} minutes, how did price move?
price_move_5way.instructions: Read `price.recent_move`. It sizes the last {window_30_min} minutes' move against the same half hour on the recent sessions and names its third. Which describes price?
criteria: price fell, a move in the top third of the recent sessions' half-hour moves at this time of day
price fell, a move in the middle third of the recent sessions' half-hour moves at this time of day
price moved either way by a move in the bottom third of the recent sessions' half-hour moves at this time of day
price rose, a move in the middle third of the recent sessions' half-hour moves at this time of day
price rose, a move in the top third of the recent sessions' half-hour moves at this time of day
code_criteria: move < 0 and |move| larger than over two thirds of the last {night_rank_count} sessions' |30-minute move| at this minute (top third)
move < 0 and |move| larger than a third to two thirds of them (middle third)
|move| larger than under a third of them (bottom third)
move > 0 and |move| larger than a third to two thirds of them (middle third)
move > 0 and |move| larger than over two thirds of them (top third)
price_move_5way.why: The single carrier of the move's sign for code to cross with other answers (so it serves direction); code also folds the options into |move| tiers for the size book, where the strong tier sharpens the flat call. It is also the reading canary: its answer key is the label's own band.

leg_vs_day_side.cadence: every 30-minute read 10:02-14:32 (sign flips into the close)
leg_vs_day_side.ask: Did the latest leg run with or against the day's side of yesterday's close?
leg_vs_day_side.instructions: Read `price.recent_move` for the last {window_30_min} minutes and `price.vs_prior_close` for where SPX sits against yesterday's close; each names its third against the same minute on the recent sessions. Check quiet first. Which describes the latest leg?

criteria.quiet: the last half hour's move is in the bottom third of the recent sessions' half-hour moves at this time of day (no real move), and price's distance from yesterday's close is in the bottom third for this time of day (near it)
criteria.quiet_leg_day_moved: the last half hour's move is in the bottom third of the recent sessions' half-hour moves at this time of day (no real move), but price's distance from yesterday's close is in the middle or top third (away from it)
criteria.leg_with_day: the last half hour's move is in the middle or top third of the recent sessions' half-hour moves at this time of day, in the same direction as the day's side of yesterday's close, and that distance is in the middle or top third
criteria.leg_against_day: the last half hour's move is in the middle or top third of the recent sessions' half-hour moves at this time of day, against the day's side of yesterday's close, and that distance is in the middle or top third
criteria.leg_on_flat_day: the last half hour's move is in the middle or top third of the recent sessions' half-hour moves at this time of day, but price's distance from yesterday's close is in the bottom third (near it)

code_criteria.quiet: |move| larger than under a third of the last {night_rank_count} sessions' |30-minute move| at this minute (bottom third), and |spot - prior_close| further than under a third of theirs at this minute (bottom third)
code_criteria.quiet_leg_day_moved: |move| in the bottom third, |spot - prior_close| in the middle or top third
code_criteria.leg_with_day: |move| in the middle or top third, |spot - prior_close| in the middle or top third, same sign
code_criteria.leg_on_flat_day: |move| in the middle or top third, |spot - prior_close| in the bottom third

leg_vs_day_side.why: The 30-minute move alone predicts almost nothing; split by the day's side measured from yesterday's close, legs with the day tend to continue and legs against it tend to fade.

move_shape.ask: How was the last half hour's move made?
move_shape.instructions: Read `price.recent_move` and `price.move_shape`. Check no_move first, then burst, then choppy. How was the last half hour's move made?

criteria.no_move: the last half hour's move is in the bottom third of the recent sessions' half-hour moves at this time of day (no real move)
criteria.burst: one five-minute stretch made most of the half hour's travel
criteria.choppy: price kept doubling back: its net move over the distance it travelled is in the bottom third of the same half hour on the recent sessions
criteria.clean: the move was spread across the half hour and went more one way than that (the middle or top third)

code_criteria.no_move: |move| larger than under a third of the last {night_rank_count} sessions' |30-minute move| at this minute (bottom third)
code_criteria.burst: largest five-minute chunk the move's way >= {move_burst_share} of the distance the six chunks travelled
code_criteria.choppy: path efficiency higher than under a third of the last {night_rank_count} sessions' 30-minute path efficiency at this minute (bottom third)

move_shape.why: Burst and choppy moves both leave price unsettled and bigger moves follow; clean moves continued before mid-afternoon and faded after, a clock interaction code weights by phase. The engine already computes path efficiency; no round-1 question read it.

one_way_hour.ask: Was the last {window_60_min} minutes one-way or two-way?
one_way_hour.instructions: Read `price.hour_one_way`. It sizes the last {window_60_min} minutes' move and counts how often price crossed its own hourly average, each against the same hour on the recent sessions. Which describes the hour?

criteria.one_way_up: price rose by a move in the middle or top third for this time of day, and crossed its hourly average less often than most recent sessions did (bottom third)
criteria.one_way_down: price fell by a move in the middle or top third for this time of day, and crossed its hourly average less often than most recent sessions did (bottom third)
criteria.two_way_up: price rose by a move in the middle or top third, but crossed its hourly average as often as usual or more (middle or top third)
criteria.two_way_down: price fell by a move in the middle or top third, but crossed its hourly average as often as usual or more (middle or top third)
criteria.no_hour_move: the hour's net move is in the bottom third of the recent sessions' hour moves at this time of day

code_criteria.one_way_up: hour move > 0, |hour move| larger than a third or more of the last {night_rank_count} sessions' |60-minute move| at this minute (middle or top third), and crosses higher than under a third of their crosses (bottom third)
code_criteria.two_way_up: hour move > 0 in the middle or top third, crosses in the middle or top third
code_criteria.no_hour_move: |hour move| larger than under a third of them (bottom third)

one_way_hour.why: An hour that moved one way without trading back through its own average has used up its one-sided flow and tends to give some back; the only chop measure that carried direction.

hour_range_vs_net.ask: Did the last half hour move, and was its range narrow or wide?
hour_range_vs_net.instructions: Read `range.hour_vs_clock` and `price.recent_move`. Decide first whether the last half hour moved: `price.recent_move` names its move's third for this time of day, and the bottom third is no real move. Which situation is it?

criteria.quiet_narrow: the last half hour's move is in the bottom third for this time of day, and the last hour's range is in the bottom or middle third for this time of day
criteria.wide_chop: the last half hour's move is in the bottom third for this time of day, but the last hour's range is in the top third for this time of day
criteria.moved_narrow: the last half hour's move is in the middle or top third for this time of day, inside an hour range in the bottom or middle third
criteria.moved_wide: the last half hour's move is in the middle or top third for this time of day, and the hour's range is in the top third

code_criteria.quiet_narrow: |30-minute move| rank below {third_lo} against the same minute on the last {night_rank_count} sessions (bottom third) and hour range rank at most {third_hi} (not the top third)
code_criteria.wide_chop: |30-minute move| rank below {third_lo} and hour range rank above {third_hi} (top third)
code_criteria.moved_narrow: |30-minute move| rank {third_lo} or more (middle or top third) and hour range rank at most {third_hi}
code_criteria.moved_wide: |30-minute move| rank {third_lo} or more and hour range rank above {third_hi}

hour_range_vs_net.why: A flat net move hides a wide two-way hour; that state is flat far less often and carries more than double the both-ways whipsaw risk, so it pushes P(flat) down and tells code to trust direction less.

day_character.cadence: every 30-minute read from 11:02, the first its label can be measured on (an hour of 5-minute returns from 10:00)
day_character.ask: So far today, are the moves building or cancelling out?
day_character.instructions: Read `price.day_character`. So far today, have half-hour stretches built on their five-minute pieces more or less than on the recent sessions at this time of day?

criteria.moves_building: the day's ratio of half-hour to five-minute moves is in the top third of the recent sessions' at this time of day
criteria.mixed: it is in the middle third
criteria.moves_cancelling: it is in the bottom third

code_criteria.moves_building: variance ratio higher than over two thirds of the last {night_rank_count} sessions' ratios at this minute (top third)
code_criteria.mixed: higher than a third to two thirds of them (middle third)
code_criteria.moves_cancelling: higher than under a third of them (bottom third)

day_character.why: A description of the day so far, not a forecast: the old 'trending / mean_reverting' names invited a continuation call the data contradicts, so the options now describe the past and code learns the sign.

groups.purpose: The gap's fate from 10:00 to mid-afternoon (signed), whether a faded gap reasserts after noon, the day's side measured from yesterday's close, the first-hour break and the noise band.

gap_side_now.ask: Is this morning's gap intact or being lost?
gap_side_now.instructions: Read `gap.size` and `gap.fill_progress`. Where price sits now decides first; the history second. Which describes the gap now?

criteria.gap_up_intact: opened above yesterday's close with a real gap (above the bottom third of the recent sessions' gaps), still keeps the half line or more of that gap, and has not touched yesterday's close
criteria.gap_up_losing: opened above with a real gap and now keeps less than the half line of it, or has touched yesterday's close
criteria.no_gap: the gap from yesterday's close was in the bottom third of the recent sessions' gaps
criteria.gap_down_losing: opened below with a real gap and now keeps less than the half line of it, or has touched yesterday's close
criteria.gap_down_intact: opened below yesterday's close with a real gap (above the bottom third of the recent sessions' gaps), still keeps the half line or more of that gap, and has not touched yesterday's close

code_criteria.gap_up_intact: gap up and |gap| beats {third_lo} or more of the last {night_rank_count} sessions' gaps (not the bottom third), share kept >= {gap_half_share}, not touched
code_criteria.gap_up_losing: gap up and not the bottom third, share kept < {gap_half_share} or touched
code_criteria.no_gap: |gap| beats under {third_lo} of the last {night_rank_count} sessions' gaps (bottom third; a tie is not beaten)

gap_side_now.why: Replaces gap_fill_state's unsigned options: 'holding' mixed gap-up and gap-down days, so the loop learned the summer's gap mix instead of the rule. Signed options each hold 15-35% of days, and the location-first wording follows the SNDK back-inside fix.

gap_fill_next_hour.cadence: every 30-minute read, awake only while code's answer key for gap_side_now is gap_up_losing or gap_down_losing (never JEV's own answer, which would be circular)
gap_fill_next_hour.sleep_when: code's answer key for gap_side_now is not gap_up_losing / gap_down_losing
gap_fill_next_hour.ask: Will price trade back to yesterday's close within the next {window_60_min} minutes?
gap_fill_next_hour.instructions: Read `gap.size`, `gap.fill_progress` and `gap.reach_distance`. Within the next {window_60_min} minutes, does price trade at or through yesterday's close?

criteria.true: price trades at or through yesterday's close within the window
criteria.false: price does not reach yesterday's close within the window

code_criteria.true: graded offline: a bar touches prior_close within {gap_touch_sigma} sigma

gap_fill_next_hour.why: A directly gradable forecast that feeds P(flat); asked only where it is uncertain.

gap_reasserts.cadence: every 30-minute read 11:32-14:32, awake only on real-gap days
gap_reasserts.ask: From the settled open to late morning, did price go with the gap or fill it?
gap_reasserts.instructions: Read `gap.size` and `gap.morning_vs_gap`. From the settled open to the late morning, did price go with this morning's gap or against it, and did it touch yesterday's close?

criteria.morning_with_gap: between the settled open and the late morning, price moved further the gap's way
criteria.morning_faded_unfilled: price moved against the gap by the late morning but never touched yesterday's close
criteria.morning_filled: price moved against the gap and touched yesterday's close by the late morning

code_criteria.morning_faded_unfilled: opposite sign, no touch of prior_close

gap_reasserts.why: Overnight gaps get pulled back early, then the direction the overnight market voted for often comes back after noon; the side lives in the label and code applies it.

day_side_from_close.cadence: every 30-minute read 10:02-14:32 (not after: the sign flips into the close)
day_side_from_close.ask: Is SPX's move from yesterday's close from the gap or built today?
day_side_from_close.instructions: Read `price.day_move_split` for how far SPX sits from yesterday's close against the same minute on the recent sessions, and how much of that came from the opening gap versus trading since the open. Check near_close first.

criteria.near_close: price's distance from yesterday's close is in the bottom third of the recent sessions' at this time of day (near it)
criteria.up_on_gap: price is above yesterday's close, price's distance from yesterday's close is in the middle or top third for this time of day, and most of it came from the opening gap
criteria.up_built_today: price is above yesterday's close, price's distance from yesterday's close is in the middle or top third for this time of day, and most of it came from trading since the open
criteria.down_on_gap: price is below yesterday's close, price's distance from yesterday's close is in the middle or top third for this time of day, and most of it came from the opening gap
criteria.down_built_today: price is below yesterday's close, price's distance from yesterday's close is in the middle or top third for this time of day, and most of it came from trading since the open

code_criteria.near_close: |spot - prior_close| further than under a third of the last {night_rank_count} sessions' at this minute (bottom third)
code_criteria.up_on_gap: above, in the middle or top third, and gap share >= {gap_half_share}, same sign
code_criteria.up_built_today: above, in the middle or top third, and gap share < {gap_half_share} or opposite sign

day_side_from_close.why: Round 1 measured the day only from the settled open, which carries no momentum on SPX; the move from yesterday's close does carry forward through midday, and the gap is the part that carries it.

first_hour_break_side.ask: What has price done with the first hour's range since?
first_hour_break_side.instructions: Read `range.first_hour`. Since the first hour ended, what has price done with its range? Where price is now decides; a price back inside counts as back inside.

criteria.inside: neither edge broken since the first hour ended
criteria.extending: one edge broken, price still beyond it, and how far it reached past that edge is in the top third of how far the recent sessions that had broken their first hour by this time of day had gone past it
criteria.stalling: one edge broken, price still beyond it, and its reach past the edge is in the bottom or middle third of the recent sessions' first-hour breaks by this time of day
criteria.failed: one edge broken, price now back inside

code_criteria.inside: no bar more than {ib_break_sigma} beyond either edge
code_criteria.extending: one side, beyond now, reach rank above {third_hi} against the furthest any bar had gone past either first-hour edge by this clock on those of the last {night_rank_count} sessions that had broken one by then, at least {same_clock_min_sessions} of them
code_criteria.stalling: one side, beyond now, reach rank at most {third_hi} against the same breaks

first_hour_break_side.why: Ten options folded to five: each mirrored pair shared one effect across two thin cells, and the loop learns direction relative to the broken edge's side (still_forming is replaced by sleeping before the first hour ends).

open_noise_band.ask: Where is price against the usual move-from-the-open band for this minute?
open_noise_band.instructions: Read `open.noise_band`. Where is price against the usual move-from-the-open band for this minute, against the same minute on the recent sessions?

criteria.at_an_edge: price has stretched past the higher or lower of the settled open and yesterday's close by a move in the middle third of the recent sessions' moves from their settled open to this minute: at the band's edge
criteria.above_band: price is above the higher of the settled open and yesterday's close by a move in the top third of the recent sessions' moves from their settled open to this minute
criteria.below_band: price is below the lower of the settled open and yesterday's close by a move in the top third of the recent sessions' moves from their settled open to this minute
criteria.inside_band: price sits between the settled open and yesterday's close, or past one of them by a move in the bottom third of the recent sessions' moves to this minute

code_criteria.at_an_edge: the stretch past the nearer of the open and yesterday's close beats {third_lo} to {third_hi} of the last {night_rank_count} sessions' moves from their settled open at this minute (middle third; a tie is not beaten)
code_criteria.above_band: above the higher of the two, the stretch beats over {third_hi} of them (top third)
code_criteria.inside_band: otherwise: between the two, or a stretch beating under {third_lo} of them (bottom third)

open_noise_band.why: A trend-versus-noise read anchored at the higher and lower of the open and yesterday's close; kept as a regime read, not as the source strategy's Sharpe. The move from the open grows with the minutes since it, so how far price has stretched past the band's anchors is judged against the same minute on the recent sessions, not against their average move and a fixed edge distance.

prior_close_push_fade.cadence: the 14:32 and 15:02 reads, awake only when the last half hour made a real move toward yesterday's close (out of the bottom third for this time of day) and price is near it (the bottom third of the same distance) or crossed it in the window
prior_close_push_fade.sleep_when: last-30 move not toward prior_close, or in the bottom third of the last {night_rank_count} sessions' |30-minute move| at this minute; or price out of the bottom third of the same distance from prior_close without a cross; or fewer than {same_clock_min_sessions} usable sessions for either rank
prior_close_push_fade.ref_side: side of yesterday's close price started from
prior_close_push_fade.ask: Where does the late push stand against yesterday's close?
prior_close_push_fade.instructions: Read `price.prior_close_push`. Price has pushed toward yesterday's close late in the day. Where does it stand against that close now?

criteria.crossed_through: price crossed yesterday's close within the last half hour and is still through it
criteria.crossed_back: price crossed yesterday's close within the last half hour but is back on its starting side
criteria.pressing_short: price has not crossed yesterday's close and is near it: its distance is in the bottom third of the recent sessions' at this time of day

code_criteria.crossed_through: crossed prior_close within {window_30_min} min, now on the far side
code_criteria.crossed_back: crossed within {window_30_min} min, now back on the starting side
code_criteria.pressing_short: no cross, |spot - prior_close| further than under a third of the last {night_rank_count} sessions' at this minute (bottom third)

prior_close_push_fade.why: Yesterday's close is the level every desk marks into the close; a late push that stalls short of it or crosses and fails is a fade setup, and one that holds through it is a flip of the day's sign.

groups.purpose: How big the next half hour will be: realized swing vs the clock, the straddle vs the clock, VIX stir, how hard the flat band is to hit, day energy and SPY's quote.

realized_vs_clock.ask: How busy was the last half hour against the same half hour on recent sessions?
realized_vs_clock.instructions: Read `vol.realized_vs_clock`. How busy was the last half hour compared with the same half hour on recent sessions? Check coiled first.

criteria.coiled: bottom fifth for this half hour and no real move inside it: its largest {window_10_min}-minute move is in the bottom third of the same half hour's largest on recent sessions
criteria.quiet: bottom fifth for this half hour, with a real move inside it: its largest {window_10_min}-minute move above the bottom third of the same half hour's largest on recent sessions
criteria.ordinary: between the top and bottom fifths: ordinary for this half hour
criteria.busy: in the top fifth, not more than every recent session: busy for this half hour
criteria.very_busy: more than every one of the recent sessions at this time of day: very busy for this half hour

code_criteria.coiled: rank <= {bottom_fifth} and the half hour's largest {window_10_min}-minute move beats under {third_lo} of the prior sessions' largest in the same half hour (bottom third)
code_criteria.quiet: rank <= {bottom_fifth} and that largest move beats at least {third_lo} of them

realized_vs_clock.why: Recent realized movement is the best single forecaster of the next half hour's size; ranking it at the same clock removes the U-shape. Dividing by the straddle (round 1) cancelled most of that information, and coil_state's fixed cuts were the clock (coiled 0% at 10:00, 37% at 14:00).

straddle_vs_clock.ask: Is the rest of today priced cheaper or richer than usual for this time of day?
straddle_vs_clock.instructions: Read `vol.straddle_vs_clock`. Compared with the same minute on the recent sessions, is the options market pricing the rest of today cheaper than usual, about usual, or richer than usual? The label's third decides.
criteria: the straddle left, as a share of the opening straddle, is in the bottom third of the recent sessions at this minute
in the middle third of the recent sessions at this minute
in the top third of the recent sessions at this minute
code_criteria: share of the prior sessions it beats < {third_lo} (bottom third)
{third_lo} <= share <= {third_hi} (middle third)
share > {third_hi} (top third)
straddle_vs_clock.why: The one home for the live straddle and the 0DTE vol pop (sigma_live over anchor correlates 0.87 with this ratio); it absorbs today_vs_month's proxy form, and a one-day VIX clause joins once that series has a same-clock baseline.

vix_stir.cadence: every 5 min 09:40-10:30 with a 10-minute window; every 30-minute read from 10:02 with a 30-minute window (the 10:02 read measures VIX since the open)
vix_stir.ask: How much has VIX moved as a share of its level?
vix_stir.instructions: Read `vol.vix_change`. Over the window the label names, how much has VIX moved, in either direction, as a share of its level, against the same window at this minute on the recent sessions? The label's band words decide.
criteria: the move is in the bottom third of the recent sessions' at this minute
in the middle third
in the top third, short of the top fifth
in the top fifth
code_criteria: |dVIX|/VIX over the window (half hour on 30-minute reads, {window_10_min} minutes in the opening lane) ranked against the same window to this minute on the prior sessions: share of them it beats < {third_lo} (bottom third)
{third_lo} <= share <= {third_hi} (middle third)
{third_hi} < share < {top_fifth} (top third, short of the top fifth)
share >= {top_fifth} (top fifth)
vix_stir.why: A VIX move adds to next-move size beyond the SPX move; fixed points break as VIX rises, so the move is a share of the level, and a share's size swings with the clock, so it is ranked against the same window at the same minute on the recent sessions (the owner's rule). vix_open_path folds in: its four-way split added nothing at 10 minutes.

flat_band_reach.horizon: 30min (asked once a read; the label's 60-minute clause is not this question's)
flat_band_reach.ask: How wide is the flat band against SPX's typical move over the horizon?
flat_band_reach.instructions: Read `ruler.flat_band_reach`. Against how far SPX typically moves over the next 30 minutes right now, does the next-30-minute flat band cover a smaller, a usual or a larger share than it did at this time of day on the recent sessions? The first clause, the 30-minute one, is ranked and decides; the 60-minute clause after it is a figure only.
criteria: the band covers less of a typical 30-minute move than on most recent sessions at this time of day (bottom third): price is more likely than usual to travel past it
the band's share of a typical 30-minute move is in the middle third of the recent sessions at this time of day
the band covers more of a typical 30-minute move than on most recent sessions at this time of day (top third): price is more likely than usual to stay inside it
code_criteria: band/reach over the next 30 minutes ranks below {third_lo} against the same share at this minute on the last {night_rank_count} sessions (bottom third)
rank {third_lo} to {third_hi} (middle third)
rank above {third_hi} (top third)
flat_band_reach.why: The flat leg is most of the up/flat/down score; the clock knows the hour but not whether today is quiet. One number tells JEV how hard 'flat' is to hit.

spx_range_pace.ask: How does today's range so far compare with a normal day's pace?
spx_range_pace.instructions: Read `range.pace_vs_priced`. The label's pace words decide. Today's range so far, measured against a one-sigma move for the time elapsed, is it under, near, over or far over the usual pace for this time of day on the recent sessions?
criteria: in the bottom third of the recent sessions at this time of day
in the middle third of the recent sessions at this time of day
in the top third of the recent sessions at this time of day, short of the top fifth
in the top fifth of the recent sessions at this time of day
code_criteria: ratio rank below {third_lo} against the same ratio at this minute on the last {night_rank_count} sessions (bottom third)
rank {third_lo} to {third_hi} (middle third)
rank above {third_hi} and below {top_fifth} (top third, not the top fifth)
rank {top_fifth} or more (top fifth)
spx_range_pace.why: Day energy. The figure is today's range over a one-sigma move from the morning ruler for the time elapsed, not 'the range the options market priced' (the ruler overstates realized about 2.5x), so the label says what it measures; its rank against the same minute on the recent sessions, not a fixed line, says whether today runs fast or slow for the hour.

spy_liquidity.ask: Is SPY's quote wider or thinner than usual for this time of day?
spy_liquidity.instructions: Read `liquidity.spy_quote`. Is SPY's quote wider, or its displayed size thinner, than usual for this time of day?

criteria.wide_spread: SPY's quoted spread, off its tightest tick, ranked in the top third of the same minute's spreads on recent sessions: wide for this time
criteria.thin_book: the spread neither wide for this time nor at the tightest tick, and the size showing at SPY's best prices in the bottom fifth for this time
criteria.tight_spread: the spread has been at its tightest tick

code_criteria.wide_spread: spread >= {spy_spread_tight}; five-minute median spread in whole cents wider than more than {third_hi} of the same minute's spreads on up to the last {night_rank_count} sessions, needing {same_clock_min_sessions} (top third; sessions at the same width tie and are not beaten)
code_criteria.thin_book: spread >= {spy_spread_tight} and its rank {third_hi} or under; size rank < {bottom_fifth}

spy_liquidity.why: The only equity liquidity read: a wide quote on the most liquid ETF means market makers are pulling back, which comes before bigger swings, clearest in the afternoon. It says nothing about direction.

straddle_repricing.ask: Did the last {window_30_min} minutes reprice the rest of today richer or cheaper than the clock?
straddle_repricing.instructions: Read `vol.straddle_reprice_30`. Over the last {window_30_min} minutes, did the options market reprice the rest of today richer or cheaper than the clock alone would have left it, against the same half hour on the recent sessions? The label's third decides.
criteria: the repricing against the clock is in the bottom third of the recent sessions' at this minute
in the middle third
in the top third
code_criteria: reprice, ranked with richer highest against the same on the prior sessions at this minute: share of them it beats < {third_lo}
{third_lo} <= share <= {third_hi}
share > {third_hi}
straddle_repricing.why: The straddle's level is straddle_vs_clock; its change against pure time decay is the market repricing the afternoon, a size read the level hides.

average_reach_30.cadence: every 30-minute read from 10:32, awake only while price is away from the day's average price (out of the bottom third of the same distance for this time of day)
average_reach_30.sleep_when: |spot - vwap| further than under a third of the last {night_rank_count} sessions' at this minute (bottom third), or fewer than {same_clock_min_sessions} usable sessions
average_reach_30.ask: Will price trade at the day's volume-weighted average within the next {window_30_min} minutes?
average_reach_30.instructions: Read `price.vs_vwap` and `price.vwap_reach`. Within the next {window_30_min} minutes, does price trade at the day's volume-weighted average price?

criteria.true: price trades at the day's average within the window
criteria.false: price does not reach the day's average within the window

code_criteria.true: graded offline: a bar's range spans vwap within {vwap_touch_sigma} sigma

average_reach_30.why: A directly gradable reach forecast for the flat bucket: the day's average is the level most intraday flow trades back to.

groups.purpose: Vol moving beyond what price explains: VIX, VVIX, the VVIX pairing with the move, the VIX9D shift, same-day skew and at-the-money IV.

vix_vs_price.ask: Did VIX move more or less fearfully than the SPX move explains?
vix_vs_price.instructions: Read `vol.vix_vs_price`. Over the last {window_30_min} minutes, did VIX move more fearfully than the SPX move alone explains, less fearfully, or in line, against the same half hour on the recent sessions? The label's third decides.

criteria.fear_ahead_of_price: VIX's leftover beyond what the SPX move explains is in the top third of the recent sessions' at this minute

code_criteria.fear_ahead_of_price: residual/VIX, ranked with VIX furthest above price highest against the same on the prior sessions at this minute: share of them it beats > {third_hi}

vix_vs_price.why: Fear showing up in VIX before price is how an unscheduled headline often appears first. Size is the stable part; the direction lean is unstable, so the why no longer calls it the best direction candidate and code learns any sign.

vvix_hidden_stir.ask: Did VVIX stir beyond what the VIX and SPX moves explain?
vvix_hidden_stir.instructions: Read `vol.vvix_vs_vix`. Over the last {window_30_min} minutes, how much did VVIX move beyond what the VIX move and the SPX move explain, either direction?

criteria.still: leftover VVIX move below the median of the same half hour's on recent sessions
criteria.stirring: leftover move between the median and the top fifth of the same half hour's on recent sessions
criteria.churning: leftover move in the top fifth of the same half hour's on recent sessions, while SPX or VIX also moved (its half-hour move above the bottom third of the recent sessions' at this minute)
criteria.churning_while_quiet: leftover move in the top fifth while SPX and VIX themselves barely moved (both half-hour moves in the bottom third of the recent sessions' at this minute)

code_criteria.still: |residual| beats under {half_rank} of the fit's |residual| over the same half hour on the prior sessions
code_criteria.churning: rank >= {top_fifth} and SPX's or VIX's half-hour move beats at least {third_lo} of the prior sessions' at this minute
code_criteria.churning_while_quiet: rank >= {top_fifth}, SPX's and VIX's half-hour moves each beat under {third_lo} of them

vvix_hidden_stir.why: Raw VVIX mostly repeats VIX (corr 0.74-0.76); the leftover flags hedging in the VIX options market that neither price nor VIX shows yet, often the first sign a pinned afternoon is about to break.

spot_vvix_pairing.ask: Did SPX move, and did VVIX rise or fall with it?
spot_vvix_pairing.instructions: Read `vol.vvix_with_move`. Do not say which way SPX went. Over the last {window_30_min} minutes, did SPX make a real move (above the bottom third of the recent sessions' half-hour moves at this minute), and did VVIX rise or fall with it?

criteria.move_vvix_up: SPX's half-hour move is above the bottom third of the recent sessions' at this minute and VVIX rose
criteria.move_vvix_down: SPX's half-hour move is above the bottom third and VVIX fell or held
criteria.no_move: SPX's half-hour move is in the bottom third of the recent sessions' at this minute

code_criteria.move_vvix_up: |SPX half-hour move| beats at least {third_lo} of the prior sessions' at this minute and VVIX change positive
code_criteria.move_vvix_down: beats at least {third_lo} of them and VVIX change zero or negative

spot_vvix_pairing.why: VIX nearly always rises on a drop, but VVIX rising or falling separates a panicked selloff (bounces) from an orderly one (continues), and flags unstable rallies. Replaces the deferred spot_vix_pairing.

front_fear_shift.ask: Did nine-day fear rise or fall against the VIX?
front_fear_shift.instructions: Read `vol.front_fear_shift`. Over the last {window_30_min} minutes, did nine-day fear rise against the VIX, fall against it, or hold, against the same half hour on the recent sessions? The label's third decides.

criteria.front_rising: nine-day VIX's shift against VIX is in the top third of the recent sessions' at this minute

code_criteria.front_rising: d(VIX9D - VIX), ranked with a gain highest against the same on the prior sessions at this minute: share of them it beats > {third_hi}

front_fear_shift.why: VIX9D's own change repeats VIX (corr 0.93) and the level gap is constant within the day; the shift in the gap is the only new intraday piece.

skew_vs_price.ask: Did downside protection get dearer or cheaper than the SPX move explains?
skew_vs_price.instructions: Read `skew.shift_vs_price`. Over the last {window_30_min} minutes, did same-day downside protection get dearer compared with upside bets by more than the SPX move alone explains, cheaper, or in line, against the same half hour on the recent sessions? The label's third decides.

criteria.puts_bid_up: the put-over-call premium's leftover beyond the SPX move is in the top third of the recent sessions' at this minute

code_criteria.puts_bid_up: residual, ranked with puts getting dearest highest against the same on the prior sessions' tapes at this minute: share of them it beats > {third_hi}

skew_vs_price.why: Traders read 'puts getting bid' as a warning; only the part price does not explain is new. It is independent of the VIX residual (corr -0.007) and leans the other way, so the two must never be blended into one 'fear' sentence.

atm_iv_vs_price.ask: Did same-day at-the-money vol move more or less than the price move explains?
atm_iv_vs_price.instructions: Read `vol.atm_iv_residual`. Did same-day at-the-money vol move more or less than the price move explains, against the same half hour on the recent sessions? The label's third decides.
criteria: vol's leftover beyond what price explains is in the top third of the recent sessions' at this minute
in the middle third
in the bottom third
code_criteria: residual, ranked with vol furthest above price highest against the same on the prior sessions at this minute: share of them it beats > {third_hi}
{third_lo} <= share <= {third_hi}
share < {third_lo}
atm_iv_vs_price.why: The 0DTE version of vix_vs_price at the hour horizon showed a clean size effect in the opposite direction: an IV bid beyond price came before calmer trading.

groups.purpose: Scheduled events and the ruler's regime: the event clock (with pre-open, 10:00 and Fed-speaker tiers), the event cycle, releases inside the lane, the loaded ruler, the vol curve and stress state.

event_clock.cadence: every 30-minute read from 10:02; in the opening lane at 09:35 and again at 10:05, after the 10:00 releases, each answer held to the next (release_in_lane carries the 10-minute clock)
event_clock.sleep_when: no scheduled event today, or every event came out beyond the digest window
event_clock.ask: Where does this moment sit against today's scheduled events?
event_clock.instructions: Read `context.event_clock`. Where does this moment sit against today's scheduled events? The first match in this order wins: due_or_under_way, released_recently, fed_speaker_window, event_later_today, released_before_open.

criteria.due_or_under_way: a major release or its follow-on is due within the due window or under way
criteria.released_recently: an in-session release or Fed remarks came out within the digest window
criteria.fed_speaker_window: a scheduled Fed official is speaking now or is due within the speaker window
criteria.event_later_today: a major event is still to come today, beyond the due window
criteria.released_before_open: today's major report came before the open and nothing major remains in session

code_criteria.due_or_under_way: major start <= now + {event_due_min} or start <= now < end
code_criteria.fed_speaker_window: fed_speaker row start <= now + {speaker_window_min} and not ended
code_criteria.released_before_open: pre_open row today, nothing in session

event_clock.why: Code needs the phase. released_before_open could never fire (the calendar left out pre-open releases); the calendar now carries pre-open, 10:00 and Fed-speaker tiers, and the Fed-speaker window is the one scheduled slice of the dark news gap.

event_cycle_day.cadence: every 30-minute read, awake only on the eve of the Fed or of a report before the open, or the day after a major release
event_cycle_day.sleep_when: no jobs report, consumer price report or Fed decision on the previous session, before the next open or at the next session (an ordinary day)
event_cycle_day.ask: Where does today sit in the cycle of major scheduled releases?
event_cycle_day.instructions: Read `calendar.event_cycle`. Where does today sit in the cycle of major scheduled releases (jobs, consumer prices, the Fed decision)? The first match in the order listed wins.

criteria.eve_of_fed: the Fed's rate decision is tomorrow
criteria.eve_of_jobs_or_cpi: the jobs report or the consumer price report comes out before tomorrow's open
criteria.day_after_event: yesterday was a major release day

code_criteria.eve_of_jobs_or_cpi: next session has JOBS or CPI pre-open
code_criteria.day_after_event: previous session had JOBS, CPI or FOMC

event_cycle_day.why: Eve afternoons trade at about a quarter of normal size and post-release sessions were among the narrowest on file; the clock and sigma cannot see tomorrow's calendar. The post_release_calm forecast folds in here.

release_in_lane.cadence: every 5 min 09:35-10:30, awake only when a release or speaker falls in the window
release_in_lane.sleep_when: nothing scheduled due within {window_10_min} minutes or started within the last {window_10_min}
release_in_lane.ask: Which scheduled release or Fed speaker falls inside this window?
release_in_lane.instructions: Read `event.release_clock_10m`. A scheduled release or Fed speaker is inside this window. Check in order: just_out, data_due_inside, speaker_due_inside.

criteria.data_due_inside: a mid-morning economic release is due inside the next window
criteria.speaker_due_inside: a scheduled Fed official's remarks start inside the next window
criteria.just_out: a release or speech started in the last window

release_in_lane.why: The lane's 10-minute size call sits across 10:00 on about a quarter of mornings; the window straddling a release is twice as big and the slots around it are not.

ruler_loaded.ask: Is today's priced move swollen or compressed, and is an event behind it?
ruler_loaded.instructions: Read `vol.ruler_event_load` with `context.event_clock`. Check in order: released_after_event, loaded_before_event, swollen_no_event, compressed, normal. Is today's options-priced move swollen by an event still to come, just released by an event that happened, swollen with no event, compressed, or normal?

criteria.loaded_before_event: the straddle prices more against the tape than on most recent sessions at this minute (top fifth), and the Fed's rate decision, the Fed chair's testimony or the Fed chair's Jackson Hole speech is still ahead today
criteria.released_after_event: the Fed's rate decision, the Fed chair's testimony or the Fed chair's Jackson Hole speech came out within the digest window and the tape now moves more against the straddle priced beforehand than on most recent sessions (their top third)
criteria.swollen_no_event: the morning ruler is in the top third of the recent sessions' morning rulers, and nothing at all is on the event calendar today: no data release and no Fed speaker either
criteria.compressed: the morning ruler is in the bottom third of the recent sessions' morning rulers

code_criteria.loaded_before_event: straddle-priced over tape-delivered half-hour move ranked at this minute: share of the prior sessions it beats >= {top_fifth}, a loading event (FOMC, Fed chair testimony, Jackson Hole) ahead
code_criteria.released_after_event: a loading event within {event_digest_min}, the tape now over the pre-event straddle ranked against the same on the prior sessions: share > {third_hi}
code_criteria.swollen_no_event: morning anchor ranked against the prior sessions' trusted anchors: share > {third_hi}, no calendar row of any kind today

ruler_loaded.why: On event days every sigma and straddle label under-reads moves before the release and over-reads after; before the release the tape is not swollen, the ruler is. Code can use the answer to trust or rescale the size answers.

thirty_minute.then: re-asked only when code sees the answer change (checked every 30 minutes)

vol_curve_vs_usual.cadence: the 10:02 read, then only when the answer changes
vol_curve_vs_usual.ask: How is the VIX curve shaped against its usual?
vol_curve_vs_usual.instructions: Read `vol.term_structure`. Check the inversions first: front_inverted, inverted. Then compared with the recent sessions at this minute, is near-term fear flatter than usual, usual, or steeper?

criteria.front_inverted: nine-day VIX at or above VIX
criteria.inverted: VIX at or above three-month VIX
criteria.flatter_than_usual: ratio in the top fifth of the recent sessions at this minute, not inverted
criteria.usual: between the top and bottom fifths of the recent sessions at this minute
criteria.steeper_than_usual: ratio in the bottom fifth of the recent sessions at this minute

vol_curve_vs_usual.why: A day-level regime read: the inversions are definitions and come first; below them the curve is judged only by its rank against the same minute on the recent sessions (the owner's rule), so the fixed near-flat line and its 'flat' option are gone; the nine-day inversion is the one inversion that actually happened.

stress_state.cadence: every 30-minute read, awake only while the stress label is written
stress_state.ask: What kind of selloff is this stress day?
stress_state.instructions: Read `vol.stress_path`. The label is written only on stress days: VIX, or its curve against three-month VIX, up from its open by more than on every recent session at this minute, VIX above their highs, or the curve at or over the inversion line. Check in order: liquidation, exhaustion, bounce_not_believed, orderly_decline. Is the selloff a liquidation, exhausting, a bounce the fear gauge does not believe, or orderly?

criteria.orderly_decline: none of the above: price lower with VIX rising roughly in line
criteria.liquidation: price at or near the session low (its distance off the low in the bottom third of the recent sessions' at this minute), VIX at new session highs, TICK repeatedly at its minute's selling burst band
criteria.exhaustion: VIX has given back a good share of its rise from the session high while SPX holds well above its low (the top third of the recent sessions' distance off the low)
criteria.bounce_not_believed: price has bounced well off its low (the top third) but VIX has not come down

code_criteria.liquidation: distance off the low beats under {third_lo} of the prior sessions' at this minute, VIX at its session high, {tick_cluster} or more NYSE TICK 1-minute lows at or past their minute's bottom burst band (the same-minute {tick_burst_pct} percentile of the prior sessions' lows, mirrored) in {window_30_min} minutes
code_criteria.exhaustion: VIX retreat share >= {stress_retreat_share} and distance off the low beats over {third_hi} of them
code_criteria.bounce_not_believed: distance off the low beats over {third_hi} of them, retreat share < {stress_hold_share}

stress_state.why: Selloff days are where intraday momentum is strongest and where a VIX retreat off the high is the classic turn; none of the 59 calm sessions reaches this state for long, so the question sleeps until it matters.

groups.purpose: The same-day book in neutral words: whether the books agree, distance to the gamma flip, the move crossed with the book, the book's calm after the late morning, the cushion and where the gamma sits in both books.

book_balance_agreement.ask: Which way do today's same-day options books lean at the current price?
book_balance_agreement.instructions: Read `gex.book_balance` and `gex.balance_vs_yesterday`. Which describes today's same-day options book at the current price? Check in order: balanced, the two split options, tipped_overnight, then the agreed options.

criteria.balanced: at least one book is too close to call
criteria.split_oi_puts_vol_calls: the open-interest book leans to puts while today's volume book leans to calls
criteria.split_oi_calls_vol_puts: the open-interest book leans to calls while today's volume book leans to puts
criteria.tipped_overnight: both books agree, but on the other side from yesterday's close
criteria.calls_heavier_both: call gamma outweighs put gamma at price in both books, same side as yesterday's close
criteria.puts_heavier_both: put gamma outweighs call gamma at price in both books, same side as yesterday's close

code_criteria.tipped_overnight: agree and differ from the prior day's last RTH regime

book_balance_agreement.why: Replaces gamma_sign_trust with words that describe what code computed (the call-vs-put gamma balance at price), so JEV's 'long gamma pins' prior never fires; split books are where reversion to VWAP and of the 30-minute move is measurable, and the two split directions are not symmetric.

flip_distance_lean.ask: How far is price from the gamma flip?
flip_distance_lean.instructions: Read `gex.flip_distance`. Do not say which side of the flip price is on. Check no_flip first, then crossed_recently, then the distance. How far is price from the gamma flip?

criteria.no_flip: no flip was found or the book is balanced
criteria.crossed_recently: price crossed the flip within the last half hour
criteria.near_flip: price's distance from the flip is in the bottom or middle third of recent sessions' at this time
criteria.far_from_flip: price's distance from the flip is in the top third of recent sessions' at this time

code_criteria.no_flip: flip null or regime uncertain (checked first)
code_criteria.crossed_recently: sign changed vs the row {window_30_min} minutes earlier (checked second)
code_criteria.near_flip: |spot - flip|/sigma ranked against the last {night_rank_count} sessions' at this minute: bottom or middle third

flip_distance_lean.why: In this data the sign is price's side of the flip, and the distance carries the direction lean the plain long/short word flattens; asking the distance removes the textbook damping prior. The deferred flip_position_cross becomes an option (crosses are rare because the flip travels with price).

rise_above_flip.ask: Did price move, and which way do the options books lean?
rise_above_flip.instructions: Read `price.recent_move` and `gex.book_balance`. Do not say which way price went. Did price make a real move for this time of day (out of the bottom third), and which way do the books lean? The criteria assume neither continuation nor reversal; code learns the mapping.

criteria.moved_calls_heavier: the last half hour's move is in the middle or top third for this time of day and both books lean to calls
criteria.moved_puts_heavier: the move is in the middle or top third and both books lean to puts
criteria.moved_books_split: the move is in the middle or top third and the books disagree or one is balanced
criteria.no_move: the move is in the bottom third of the recent sessions' half-hour moves at this time of day

code_criteria.moved_calls_heavier: |move| larger than a third or more of the last {night_rank_count} sessions' |30-minute move| at this minute (middle or top third), both long
code_criteria.moved_puts_heavier: |move| in the middle or top third, both short
code_criteria.moved_books_split: |move| in the middle or top third, split/uncertain
code_criteria.no_move: |move| larger than under a third of them (bottom third)

rise_above_flip.why: The single cross of the move with the book. It repeats much of the move (NMI 0.865), but the one cell that separates is measurable, and the split cells now carry a side because under split books the move reverses.

book_vs_pace.cadence: every 30-minute read from 11:32 (asleep before the late-morning gate)
book_vs_pace.ask: How does the options book's balance pair with the pace?
book_vs_pace.instructions: Read `gex.book_balance` and `vol.realized_vs_clock_rank`. The label's third decides the pace: top third is fast. Which pairing is it?

criteria.calls_heavier_normal: both books lean to calls and the last half hour's pace is not in the top third of the recent sessions' for its clock
criteria.calls_heavier_hot: both lean to calls and the last half hour's pace is in the top third
criteria.puts_heavier_hot: both lean to puts and the pace is in the top third
criteria.puts_heavier_normal: both lean to puts and the pace is not in the top third
criteria.split: the books disagree or one is balanced

code_criteria.calls_heavier_normal: both long, the last half hour's realized swing beats at most {third_hi} of the prior sessions' at this minute
code_criteria.calls_heavier_hot: both long, beats over {third_hi} of them
code_criteria.puts_heavier_hot: both short, beats over {third_hi} of them
code_criteria.puts_heavier_normal: both short, beats at most {third_hi} of them
