book_vs_pace.why: The book's calming effect exists only after the opening hours; asking it all day blurred it into nothing, which made the sign look inverted. The pace input is now the last half hour, not the whole day's pace.

gamma_cushion.ask: How much room does the book's balance have before it tips?
gamma_cushion.instructions: Read `gex.cushion_if_moved`. Check puts_heavier_now first. Which describes how much room the book's balance has before it tips?
gamma_cushion.dark_reason: the row carries no cushion: sliding the gamma flip by half a sigma needs the full options chain, which the scan has and the diary does not write (gex_views.cushion_up and cushion_down)

criteria.puts_heavier_now: put gamma already outweighs call gamma at price
criteria.sturdy: a move either way leaves the book call-heavy with room to spare
criteria.thin_below: a drop leaves it call-heavy but under the thin line; a rise holds
criteria.tips_below: a drop would tip the balance to puts; a rise holds
criteria.soft_above: a rise would thin or tip the balance; a drop holds
criteria.soft_both: moves either way thin or tip the balance

code_criteria.sturdy: both sides keep >= {cushion_thin} of today's level

gamma_cushion.why: It serves size, not direction: when only a drop would tip the book the next hour ran wider, with no direction lean. Worded as the balance tipping, not dealers flipping.

gamma_weight_both_books.ask: Where does the gamma sit in today's book and the week's?
gamma_weight_both_books.instructions: Read `gex.weight_both_books`. The label's third words decide. Against the same books on recent sessions at this time, does today's same-day book and the 1-to-7-day book (today's expiry excluded) hold more of its gamma above price than usual, more below, or about as usual? A book's share above price can be in the top third and still be under half: the thirds say more than usual, not which side holds most.

criteria.both_below: both books' share of gamma above price is in the bottom third of recent sessions' at this time: both hold more of their gamma below price than usual
criteria.both_above: both books' share above price is in the top third: both hold more of their gamma above price than usual
criteria.week_below_today_not: the 1-to-7-day book holds more of its gamma below price than usual (bottom third); today's book is in the middle or top third
criteria.week_above_today_not: the 1-to-7-day book holds more of its gamma above price than usual (top third); today's book is in the middle or bottom third
criteria.week_even: the 1-to-7-day book's share above price is in the middle third: about as usual

code_criteria.both_below: both shares above price ranked against the last {night_rank_count} sessions' at this minute: bottom third
code_criteria.week_below_today_not: week bottom third, today middle or top third
code_criteria.week_above_today_not: week top third, today middle or bottom third

gamma_weight_both_books.why: Before noon today's same-day book holds about a third of the gamma dealers hedge; the week's book fires on more days and disagrees with today's on a third of reads. No 'lid or floor' wording: the two old texts contradicted each other. Each book is now judged by its third against the same book at this minute on recent sessions (owner rule 2026-09-27), not the 40%-60% even band the evidence was measured on: more above or below price than usual, never which side holds most.

groups.purpose: The book's structure against price: magnet seat, wall box, wall motion, wall touches, strike defense, and VWAP stretch crossed with book agreement.

magnet_seat.ask: Is price seated on today's heaviest strike, near it, or away?

criteria.held_on_magnet: price is seated on the heaviest strike (its distance in the bottom third of recent sessions' at this time), over the last half hour it sat closer to it than on most recent sessions (bottom third), it is the same strike, and its grip is at or above the median for this time of day
criteria.seated_fresh: seated now (bottom third), but the last half hour was not held there, or the strike just changed, or the grip is below the median
criteria.near: the heaviest strike's distance is in the middle third of recent sessions' at this time
criteria.away: the heaviest strike's distance is in the top third of recent sessions' at this time

code_criteria.held_on_magnet: distance rank bottom third, the half hour's mean distance rank bottom third, same strike, grip rank >= {half_rank}

magnet_seat.why: The one tradeability signal that beats the clock on SPX: a seated, gripping pin means a flatter next half hour. It is a speed limit, not a magnet, until the last half hour (see settle_pull_side). Grip is ranked at the same clock because it climbs all day.

wall_box.ask: How tight is the box between the heaviest call-side and put-side strikes?
wall_box.instructions: Read `gex.wall_box` and `gex.walls_since_30min`. Which describes the box between the heaviest call-side and put-side strikes?

criteria.tight_standing: the two heavy strikes are closer together than on most recent sessions at this time (bottom third) and unchanged for the last half hour
criteria.tight_redrawing: bottom third, but a heavy strike just changed
criteria.middling: the width is in the middle third of recent sessions' at this time
criteria.wide: the width is in the top third

code_criteria.tight_standing: width rank against the last {night_rank_count} sessions at this minute bottom third, unchanged for {window_30_min}

wall_box.why: A tight standing box is a quiet read; the morning/later split re-asked the clock that code already blends, so it is gone.

walls_motion.ask: How did the heaviest strikes move over the last {window_30_min} minutes?
walls_motion.instructions: Read `gex.walls_since_30min`. Check both_moved_up and both_moved_down first. Over the last {window_30_min} minutes, how did the heaviest call-side and put-side strikes move?

criteria.both_moved_up: both heavy strikes are now at higher strikes
criteria.both_moved_down: both heavy strikes are now at lower strikes
criteria.pulled_in: the two heavy strikes are closer together
criteria.spread_out: the two heavy strikes are further apart
criteria.stood_still: both heavy strikes are where they were

code_criteria.pulled_in: call down or put up, gap narrower

walls_motion.why: Keeps the one part of walls_vs_move that changes within the day and drops the repeat of the move (77% of its answers were no_move); code crosses it with the move.

wall_touch_effort.cadence: every 30-minute read, awake only when a wall or the magnet was touched in the last half hour
wall_touch_effort.ask: What happened at the heavy strike price touched?
wall_touch_effort.instructions: Read `levels.wall_touch_effort`. Check the break and hold options first. What happened at the heavy strike price touched?

criteria.broke_through_call_side: price went through the call-side heavy strike above and stayed through
criteria.broke_through_put_side: price went through the put-side heavy strike below and stayed through
criteria.held_at_call_side: price tested the call-side heavy strike and pulled back down
criteria.held_at_put_side: price tested the put-side heavy strike and pulled back up
criteria.touching_heavy_effort: touching now with SPY volume in the top band for these minutes
criteria.touching_light_effort: touching now with SPY volume in the middle or bottom band

code_criteria.broke_through_call_side: closed beyond by > {wall_touch_sigma} and still beyond

wall_touch_effort.why: Signed options so the loop learns direction; no_touch (78% of reads) is removed by gating, so the default answer never enters the weights.

strike_defense.cadence: every 30-minute read, awake only when a contested strike is within reach: its distance from price not in the top third of the nearest contested strike's distance at this minute on recent sessions
strike_defense.ask: Are market makers defending the nearest heavily hit strike or leaving it?
strike_defense.instructions: Read `options.strike_defense`. At the nearest strike within reach where same-day quotes keep getting hit, are market makers putting quotes back more or less than usual for this time, and is it above or below price?

criteria.defended_above: contested strike above price, its refill share at or above the middle of the same minute's refill shares on recent sessions
criteria.abandoned_above: contested strike above price, its refill share below the middle
criteria.defended_below: contested strike below price, its refill share at or above the middle
criteria.abandoned_below: contested strike below price, its refill share below the middle

code_criteria.defended_above: >= {defense_min_events} hits; distance from price not in the top third of the nearest contested strike's distance at this minute on up to the last {night_rank_count} sessions (rank {third_hi} or under), needing {same_clock_min_sessions}; refill share higher than at least {half_rank} of those sessions' refill shares at this minute

strike_defense.why: The only order-book read with any support here; it reads the options book's refill, not SPY's top of book.

vwap_side_vs_books.ask: Which side of the day's average price is SPX, and do the books agree?
vwap_side_vs_books.instructions: Read `price.vs_vwap` and `gex.book_balance`. The opening words of each label decide. Check near_average first. Which situation is it?

criteria.near_average: price's distance from the day's average price is in the bottom third of the recent sessions' at this time of day (at the average)
criteria.above_books_agree: price is above the day's average, price's distance from the day's average price is in the middle or top third of the recent sessions' at this time of day, and both books lean the same way
criteria.above_books_split: above it, price's distance from the day's average price is in the middle or top third of the recent sessions' at this time of day, and the books disagree or one is balanced
criteria.below_books_agree: below it, price's distance from the day's average price is in the middle or top third of the recent sessions' at this time of day, and both books lean the same way
criteria.below_books_split: below it, price's distance from the day's average price is in the middle or top third of the recent sessions' at this time of day, and the books disagree or one is balanced

code_criteria.near_average: |spot - vwap| further than under a third of the last {night_rank_count} sessions' at this minute (bottom third)
code_criteria.above_books_agree: above, middle or top third, regime == volume book, neither uncertain
code_criteria.above_books_split: above, middle or top third, split or uncertain

vwap_side_vs_books.why: Every option carries a side. Whether a departure from the average comes back depends on the books agreeing, not on the long/short word, which just repeats which side of the flip price is on. The stretch size and minutes since the last touch ride in the label.

groups.purpose: Where price sits against yesterday's value area and range, round levels, armed breaks, the overnight range, and heavy trading that is not moving price.

prior_value_location.ask: Where is price against yesterday's value area, and which way is today going?
prior_value_location.instructions: Read `levels.prior_value` for where price sits against the band where SPX spent most of yesterday's session, and `price.day_move` for which way today has gone since the settled open and that move's third for this time of day (the bottom third counts as flat). Pick the option that matches both.

criteria.below_value_rallying: price is below yesterday's value band even though today is up or flat (a move from the settled open in the bottom third for this time of day)
criteria.below_value_falling: price is below yesterday's value band and today is down by a move in the middle or top third for this time of day
criteria.above_value_rising: price is above yesterday's value band and today is up or flat
criteria.above_value_slipping: price is above yesterday's value band but today is down by a move in the middle or top third for this time of day
criteria.inside_value: price is inside, or within the edge distance of, yesterday's value band

code_criteria.below_value_rallying: more than {value_edge_sigma} below the value-area low; day move from the settled open up, or down with its size ranked below {third_lo} against the same move at this minute on the last {night_rank_count} sessions
code_criteria.below_value_falling: same location; day move down with its size rank {third_lo} or more
code_criteria.above_value_rising: more than {value_edge_sigma} above the high; day move up, or down with its size rank below {third_lo}
code_criteria.above_value_slipping: same location; day move down with its size rank {third_lo} or more
code_criteria.inside_value: inside, or within {value_edge_sigma} of, the band

prior_value_location.why: Traders judge acceptance against yesterday's fair value. Today's move alone predicts nothing here, but a rally that stays below yesterday's value tends to fail and strength above value tends to keep going. Round 1 used only yesterday's high and low.

prior_day_acceptance.ask: What is price doing at yesterday's high or low?
prior_day_acceptance.instructions: Read `levels.prior_day`. Where price is now decides first. Check in order: rejected_back_inside, accepted_beyond, testing_edge, inside_away. Which situation is it at yesterday's high or low?

criteria.rejected_back_inside: price poked beyond yesterday's high or low and is now back inside
criteria.accepted_beyond: price is beyond yesterday's high or low now and has been beyond it for at least the acceptance time
criteria.testing_edge: price is within reach of yesterday's high or low, or beyond it for less than the acceptance time
criteria.inside_away: inside yesterday's range, away from both edges

code_criteria.testing_edge: within {level_reach_sigma} of an edge, or beyond for < {accept_minutes} minutes

prior_day_acceptance.why: Folded: the high and low mirrors share one table with direction learned relative to the edge's side (named in the label), and the location-first wording avoids the SNDK back-inside misread.

round_level_cross.cadence: every 30-minute read and every 5-minute lane read, awake only near or just through a round level
round_level_cross.ask: Has price just crossed a round level, or is it pressing one?
round_level_cross.instructions: Read `levels.round_number`. Has price just pushed through a round level, or is it pressing one without crossing?

criteria.just_crossed_up: within the cross window price rose through a round level and is still above it
criteria.just_crossed_down: within the cross window price fell through a round level and is still below it
criteria.pressing_from_below: price is just under a round level it has not crossed
criteria.pressing_from_above: price is just over a round level it has not broken

code_criteria.just_crossed_up: level inside a bar's range within {cross_lookback_min} min, price {round_near_sigma}+ below it before, above now

round_level_cross.why: Almost every SPX trader marks the big round numbers; order data shows stops cluster just past them and speed the move once crossed. The levels are also the big SPXW strikes, so it goes on the overlap list with the wall questions.

break_armed.cadence: every 30-minute read from 10:02, awake only while a break is armed or recently expired
break_armed.sleep_when: break_state idle and nothing expired or decocked within {window_30_min} minutes
break_armed.ask: Is a level-break setup armed, and which way?
break_armed.instructions: Read `levels.break_armed`. Is a level-break setup armed right now, and which way? The opening words decide.

criteria.armed_up: a break upward through a nearby level is armed and has not fired or expired
criteria.armed_down: a break downward through a nearby level is armed and has not fired or expired
criteria.recently_expired: an armed break expired or was called off within the last half hour

break_armed.why: The station arms this setup only when the book leans to puts and price was just turned back at a named level; its direction comes from the level, not the last move, and it survives a momentum control. It is the usable part of level_reclaim, which never fired.

overnight_range_position.ask: Where is price against the overnight futures range?
overnight_range_position.instructions: Read `overnight.range` and `overnight.price_vs_range`. Where price is now decides first. Check in order: above, below, the two back-inside options, near an edge, middle.
overnight_range_position.dark_reason: the overnight store (state/spx_jev/overnight/, saved at 09:26 ET) holds /ES's bars, but no session read measures the night's range from them yet

criteria.above_overnight_high: now more than the break distance above the overnight high
criteria.below_overnight_low: now more than the break distance below the overnight low
criteria.inside_now_after_breaking_above: inside the overnight range now after trading above its high earlier today (the open counts)
criteria.inside_now_after_breaking_below: inside now after trading below its low earlier today
criteria.inside_near_edge: no break today, inside or within the break distance of an overnight edge, within the near distance
criteria.inside_middle: no break today, away from both edges

code_criteria.inside_near_edge: inside or up to {on_break_sigma} beyond, within {on_near_sigma} of an edge

overnight_range_position.why: Futures traders watch the overnight edges; one question with one buffer instead of two, and the open location becomes the earlier-break history. Needs the new /ESZ26 overnight save job.

activity_vs_move.ask: Did option or SPY activity come with a price move?
activity_vs_move.instructions: Read `options.premium_pace_30`, `volume.spy_pace_30` and `price.recent_move`. Use the premium label; use SPY volume only when the premium label is absent. Which pairing is it?

criteria.heavy_no_move: trading in the top fifth for this time of day while price's 30-minute move ranked in the bottom third for this minute: no real move
criteria.heavy_with_move: trading in the top fifth and price's 30-minute move ranked above the bottom third for this minute
criteria.light: trading in the bottom fifth, whatever price did

code_criteria.heavy_no_move: pace rank >= {top_fifth}, 30-minute move rank below {third_lo} (bottom third)
code_criteria.heavy_with_move: pace rank >= {top_fifth}, 30-minute move rank {third_lo} or above (middle or top third)

activity_vs_move.why: Heavy trading that is not moving price is absorption; unproven, so it stays live and goes on the overlap list with realized_vs_clock.

groups.purpose: NYSE and S&P-member breadth: agreement with the move (sign-free), the day's breadth regime, TICK against its usual, unconfirmed extremes (with IWM) and members vs price and vs NYSE.

breadth_agrees_with_move.ask: Does breadth side with the last half hour's move?
breadth_agrees_with_move.instructions: Read `price.recent_move` and `breadth.net_volume_change_30m`. Do not say which way price went; say only whether breadth sides with the move. A real move is one outside the bottom third of the same half hour on recent sessions; NYSE net volume's change over the half hour leans by its third against the same half hour on recent sessions (top third to buying, bottom third to selling). Which describes it?

criteria.agrees_with_move: price made a real move, and NYSE net volume's 30-minute change leans the same way (in the top third on a rise, the bottom third on a fall)
criteria.against_move: price made a real move, and NYSE net volume's 30-minute change leans the opposite way
criteria.move_without_breadth: price made a real move, and NYSE net volume's 30-minute change ranks in the middle third
criteria.breadth_leans_price_still: price made no real move (bottom third), but NYSE net volume's 30-minute change ranks in the top or bottom third
criteria.both_quiet: no real move, and NYSE net volume's 30-minute change ranks in the middle third

code_criteria.agrees_with_move: |30-minute move| not in the bottom third of the same half hour on the prior sessions (move_rank); NYSE net volume's 30-minute change ($VOLD now less $VOLD 30 minutes ago) in the top third on a rise or the bottom third on a fall, ranked signed against the same change at this minute on up to the last {night_rank_count} sessions (at least {same_clock_min_sessions}, else the label is omitted and the question skipped)
code_criteria.move_without_breadth: a real move, the net volume change in the middle third
code_criteria.breadth_leans_price_still: move in the bottom third, the net volume change in the top or bottom third

breadth_agrees_with_move.why: Template for every 'X vs the move' cross: sign-free options leave direction to price_move_5way alone, so the combiner does not count the move again inside each cross (SNDK closes_agree was retired for exactly this). Code multiplies agree/against by the move's sign.

breadth_day_regime.ask: Since the open, has volume been lopsided, rotating or leaning?
breadth_day_regime.instructions: Read `breadth.day_upvol_share`. Apply in order and take the first that fits. Since the open, has volume been lopsided against recent sessions at this minute, faded from lopsided, rotating, or leaning?

criteria.one_sided_up: today's share of volume in rising stocks ranks in the top fifth of the same share at this minute on recent sessions, and the sign switches of the half hours' NYSE net volume changes do not rank in the top third
criteria.one_sided_down: the share ranks in the bottom fifth, and the sign switches do not rank in the top third
criteria.faded_from_one_side: the share stood in the top or bottom fifth at an earlier half hour's mark today (ranked at that mark) and now ranks in the middle third
criteria.rotational: the sign switches of the half hours' NYSE net volume changes rank in the top third of the same count by this minute on recent sessions: a range day

code_criteria.one_sided_up: day share rank >= {top_fifth}, sign switches rank not above {third_hi}
code_criteria.one_sided_down: day share rank <= {bottom_fifth}, sign switches rank not above {third_hi}
code_criteria.faded_from_one_side: an earlier half hour's mark ranked at or past a fifth, now the middle third
code_criteria.rotational: sign switches higher than more than {third_hi} of the prior sessions' by this minute (top third)

breadth_day_regime.why: A rotating-day read for the flat bucket; unproven, so live.

tick_lean_vs_usual.ask: Did the NYSE tick lean to buying or selling more than usual for this half hour?
tick_lean_vs_usual.instructions: Read `breadth.tick_side_vs_usual`. Compared with the same half hour on recent sessions, did the NYSE tick sit above zero more often, less often, or about as usual? The rank's level decides.
criteria: the share of minutes above zero ranks in the bottom fifth of the same share at this minute on recent sessions
in the bottom third, short of the bottom fifth
in the middle third
in the top third, short of the top fifth
in the top fifth
code_criteria: rank <= {bottom_fifth}
{bottom_fifth} < rank, below the bottom-third edge (higher than fewer than {third_lo} of the prior sessions)
middle third
above the top-third edge (higher than more than {third_hi}), rank < {top_fifth}
rank >= {top_fifth}
tick_lean_vs_usual.why: Two questions counted the same TICK side, and raw TICK sits below zero most of the time (median share above zero 0.33), so both answered 'selling' in a rising market. One question, measured against the usual for the clock.

new_extreme_unconfirmed.cadence: every 30-minute read, awake only when SPX set a new session extreme within the recent window
new_extreme_unconfirmed.ask: Did breadth confirm SPX's new session extreme?
new_extreme_unconfirmed.instructions: Read `price.session_extreme_recent` and `breadth.at_extremes`. SPX just set a new session high or low; do not say which. Did NYSE net volume reach its level at the previous extreme, and were small caps as close to their own extreme as usual, in the bottom third of the same distance on recent sessions at that minute?

criteria.extreme_confirmed: NYSE net volume reached its level at the previous extreme, and small caps' (IWM) distance from their own extreme ranks in the bottom third of the same distance at that minute on recent sessions
criteria.extreme_unconfirmed: NYSE net volume fell short of its level at the previous extreme, or small caps' distance ranks in the middle or top third

code_criteria.extreme_confirmed: VOLD at or past its level at the previous extreme and IWM's distance from its own extreme, in SPX sigma, higher than fewer than {third_lo} of the prior sessions' same distance at the extreme's minute (bottom third; each session in its own ruler, at least {same_clock_min_sessions})

new_extreme_unconfirmed.why: The classic narrow-push tell. The megacap basket almost never splits (QQQ confirmed 97 of 101 SPX highs), while small caps split about in half, so IWM replaces it; no_new_extreme is removed by gating.

member_breadth_vs_price_day.ask: Is SPX's move since the open backed by net buying in its own stocks?
member_breadth_vs_price_day.instructions: Read `price.day_move` and `breadth.members_net_day`. Is SPX's move since the open backed by net buying volume in S&P 500 stocks, or does that volume point the other way? A move counts once it ranks outside the bottom third of the same move from the settled open at this minute on recent sessions.

criteria.up_backed: SPX is above its settled open by a move outside the bottom third of recent sessions' at this minute, and S&P 500 net volume is positive
criteria.up_unbacked: SPX is above the open by a move outside the bottom third, but S&P 500 net volume is zero or negative
criteria.down_backed: SPX is below the open by a move outside the bottom third, and net volume is negative
criteria.down_unbacked: SPX is below the open by a move outside the bottom third, but net volume is zero or positive
criteria.near_open: SPX's move from the settled open ranks in the bottom third

code_criteria.up_backed: day move up, |day move| not in the bottom third (move_rank over the minutes since 09:35), members' net volume positive
code_criteria.up_unbacked: day move up, not in the bottom third, members' net volume zero or negative
code_criteria.near_open: |day move| in the bottom third (checked first)

member_breadth_vs_price_day.why: A day move made on the members' own net selling is carried by a few heavy names or futures, and it stalled or turned more often. $VOLSPD is S&P 500 up-minus-down volume, not Nasdaq breadth as round 1 and the feed probe said.

member_vs_nyse_breadth.ask: Has net volume in S&P 500 stocks been stronger or weaker than across the NYSE?
member_vs_nyse_breadth.instructions: Read `breadth.members_net_day`. The label's thirds decide. Since the open, compared with the same minute on recent sessions, has net volume in S&P 500 stocks been stronger, weaker, or matched against all NYSE stocks?

criteria.members_stronger: S&P 500 net volume ranks in a higher third of recent sessions at this minute than NYSE-wide net volume does
criteria.members_weaker: it ranks in a lower third
criteria.matched: both rank in the same third

code_criteria.members_stronger: third(VOLSPD) above third(VOLD), each ranked against the same measure at this minute on up to the last {night_rank_count} sessions (at least {same_clock_min_sessions}, else the label is omitted and the question skipped)

member_vs_nyse_breadth.why: The two tallies usually agree (0.91); when the index's own members lag the whole exchange, big-cap selling is hidden by ADRs, funds and smaller listings.

breadth_flip_after_release.cadence: every 30-minute read, awake only within the digest window after an in-session release
breadth_flip_after_release.ask: Since the release, has NYSE volume switched sides?
breadth_flip_after_release.instructions: Read `breadth.flip_after_release`. Since this session's release, has NYSE net volume switched sides against the hour before it? Each window's change in NYSE net volume leans by its third against the same minutes on recent sessions, release or not.

criteria.flipped_to_buying: in the bottom third before the release, in the top third since
criteria.flipped_to_selling: in the top third before the release, in the bottom third since
criteria.kept_side: in the same top or bottom third before and since the release
criteria.no_clear_side: in the middle third before or since the release

code_criteria.flipped_to_buying: before rank higher than fewer than {third_lo} of the prior sessions over the same minutes (bottom third), since rank higher than more than {third_hi} (top third)
code_criteria.flipped_to_selling: before top third, since bottom third
code_criteria.kept_side: the same outer third both times

breadth_flip_after_release.why: A release that flips which stocks carry the volume has changed the day's story; one that leaves the breadth side alone was noise.

volume_vs_count.ask: Did volume run heavier in rising or falling stocks than their count suggests?
volume_vs_count.instructions: Read `breadth.volume_vs_count_30m`. Over the last {window_30_min} minutes, compared with the same half hour on recent sessions, did volume run heavier in rising stocks than their count would suggest, heavier in falling stocks, or matched as usual?

criteria.volume_ahead_rising: mean TRIN over the half hour ranks in the bottom third of the same mean at this minute on recent sessions: volume leaned to rising stocks beyond their count
criteria.volume_ahead_falling: mean TRIN ranks in the top third
criteria.matched: mean TRIN ranks in the middle third

code_criteria.volume_ahead_rising: mean TRIN higher than fewer than {third_lo} of the prior sessions at this minute (bottom third), ranked against the same measure at this minute on up to the last {night_rank_count} sessions (at least {same_clock_min_sessions}, else the label is omitted and the question skipped)
code_criteria.volume_ahead_falling: higher than more than {third_hi} of them (top third)

volume_vs_count.why: TRIN's information that up-volume share and the advance count each miss: whether the money is concentrated on one side.

groups.purpose: Who carries the index: equal weight (beta-adjusted), semis, sectors, the megacaps' cohesion, top-8 vs the rest, and QQQ vs IWM over the day.

move_breadth.ask: Did the typical stock move with the index, or did the biggest stocks carry it?
move_breadth.instructions: Read `price.recent_move` and `leaders.equal_weight_vs_cap_30m`. Over the last {window_30_min} minutes, after allowing for equal weight's usual swing, did the typical stock move with the index, or did the biggest stocks carry it?

criteria.broad: the index moved (above the bottom third of recent sessions at this time) and the typical stock kept up: its split from its usual multiple was not both top-third in size and against the move
criteria.narrow: the index moved but the typical stock lagged it: its split was in the top third by size and against the move
criteria.hidden_move: the index did not move (bottom third) but the typical stock split from it by a top-third margin
criteria.no_move: the index did not move and the split was not in the top third

code_criteria.broad: price.recent_move's {window_30_min}-minute move ranks above the bottom third of the same half hour on the recent sessions; the RSP-vs-SPY residual not (top third by size and against the move)
code_criteria.narrow: price.recent_move's {window_30_min}-minute move ranks above the bottom third of the same half hour on the recent sessions; |residual| in the top third of the same half hour's on the recent sessions (rank >= {third_hi}), against the move
code_criteria.hidden_move: price.recent_move's {window_30_min}-minute move is in the bottom third of the same half hour on the recent sessions; |residual| in the top third

move_breadth.why: Beta-adjusted: raw RSP moves only 0.66x SPY, so the raw gap made every big move look narrow. Sign-free so the move is not counted twice.

semis_tell.ask: Did semiconductors run ahead of the index, and which way?
semis_tell.instructions: Read `leaders.semis_vs_index_30m` and `price.recent_move`. After allowing for chips usually moving further than the index, did semis run ahead upward, ahead downward, in line, or stay quiet?

criteria.ahead_up: chips beat their usual multiple of the index by a top-fifth margin for this half hour
criteria.ahead_down: chips trailed their usual multiple by a bottom-fifth margin
criteria.in_line: the index moved (above the bottom third of recent sessions at this time) and chips moved about their usual multiple
criteria.quiet: the index did not move (bottom third) and chips did nothing beyond their usual multiple

code_criteria.in_line: price.recent_move's {window_30_min}-minute move ranks above the bottom third of the same half hour on the recent sessions; residual between the fifths
code_criteria.quiet: price.recent_move's {window_30_min}-minute move is in the bottom third of the same half hour on the recent sessions; residual between the fifths

semis_tell.why: Chips lead the AI-weighted index; the side is in the option, not a product with the move.

sector_agreement.ask: Did the sector funds move together with the index?
sector_agreement.instructions: Read `sectors.agreement_30m` and `price.recent_move`. Over the last {window_30_min} minutes, did the sector funds move together with the index, only partly, or swap places under a flat index?

criteria.one_way: the index moved and more sector funds went its way, each by a move above the bottom third of its own at this time, than on most recent sessions (the count in the top third)
criteria.patchy_move: the index moved but the count of funds going with it was not in the top third
criteria.rotation_under_flat: the index barely moved but the sector funds split apart by a top-third dispersion
criteria.quiet: the index barely moved and the sectors did not split apart

code_criteria.one_way: price.recent_move's {window_30_min}-minute move ranks above the bottom third of the same half hour on the recent sessions; the count of funds moving the index's way by a move above the bottom third of their own at this minute ranks in the top third (rank >= {third_hi}, ties not beaten)
code_criteria.patchy_move: price.recent_move's {window_30_min}-minute move ranks above the bottom third of the same half hour on the recent sessions; the count below the top third
code_criteria.rotation_under_flat: price.recent_move's {window_30_min}-minute move is in the bottom third of the same half hour on the recent sessions; dispersion in the top third

sector_agreement.why: Index variance is component variance times correlation; rotation under a flat index is the best-grounded chop idea outside price.

megacap_cohesion.ask: How did the largest index stocks move together over the last {window_30_min} minutes?
megacap_cohesion.instructions: Read `leaders.megacap_cohesion_30m`. Check in order: one_name, together_up, together_down, cancelling, drifting. How did the largest index stocks move over the last {window_30_min} minutes?
megacap_cohesion.dark_reason: the index weights of its largest stocks (state/spx_leaders/weights.json), which nothing writes yet

criteria.one_name: one big stock supplied more than the one-name share of a real index move (above the bottom third of recent sessions at this time); this answer comes first, whatever the other giants did
criteria.together_up: no one stock carried a real move, and more of the {mega_count} largest rose than fell, each by a move above the bottom third of its own at this time, with that count in the top third of recent sessions
criteria.together_down: no one stock carried a real move, and more fell than rose, each by a move above the bottom third of its own, with that count in the top third
criteria.cancelling: neither of the above, and at least two giants moved each way, each by a move above the bottom third of its own, cancelling
criteria.drifting: none of the above: the giants were mostly quiet or patternless

code_criteria.one_name: one name's contribution > {mega_one_name_share} of an index move ranked above the bottom third at this minute (the label: past the one-name share, and a real move); checked first
code_criteria.together_up: not one_name; the larger of the up and down counts (a name counts when its move is above the bottom third of its own at this minute) ranks in the top third of the same count on the last {night_rank_count} sessions (rank >= {third_hi}, ties not beaten), and more up than down (the label: moving together up)
code_criteria.cancelling: not one_name and not together_up or together_down; two or more up and two or more down, each above the bottom third of its own

megacap_cohesion.why: Concentration flag. one_name almost never fired at the old rule (1.5% of windows); the basket now comes from weights, with TSLA in and Alphabet's two share classes combined.

leaders_vs_rest.ask: Which part of the index did the moving over the last {window_30_min} minutes?
leaders_vs_rest.instructions: Read `leaders.pull_vs_rest_30m`. Over the last {window_30_min} minutes, which part of the index did the moving: the largest names, the rest, both the same way, or the two pulling against each other?
leaders_vs_rest.dark_reason: the index weights of its largest stocks (state/spx_leaders/weights.json), which nothing writes yet

criteria.leaders_carry_up: the largest names' pull moved the index up (above the bottom third of recent sessions at this time) and the rest's stayed in the bottom third
criteria.leaders_carry_down: the largest names' pull moved it down and the rest's stayed in the bottom third
criteria.rest_carries: the rest's pull moved (above the bottom third) while the largest names' stayed in the bottom third
criteria.together: both parts moved, above the bottom third, the same way
criteria.tug_of_war: both parts moved, above the bottom third, in opposite directions
criteria.quiet: neither part moved: both in the bottom third

code_criteria.leaders_carry_up: |largest names' contribution| ranks above the bottom third of the same on the last {night_rank_count} sessions at this minute (rank >= {third_lo}), up; the rest's in the bottom third
code_criteria.rest_carries: the rest's above the bottom third, the largest names' in it
code_criteria.together: both above the bottom third, same sign
code_criteria.tug_of_war: both above the bottom third, opposite

leaders_vs_rest.why: Cap-weighted split: is one group the index today. A tug of war under a pinned index is megacap_pull_at_pin's case, now crossed by code with magnet_seat instead of a pin-gated question that was not_pinned on over 95% of reads.

size_leadership_day.cadence: every 30-minute read from 10:32 (signal measured from 12:00; asked earlier so the weights learn the morning is weak)
size_leadership_day.ask: Since the open, have tech or small caps led the index?
size_leadership_day.instructions: Read `leaders.size_spread_day`. Since the settled open, after allowing for each fund's usual swing against SPY, which group has led: the Nasdaq-100 fund QQQ, the small-cap fund IWM, both, one ahead and one behind, or neither?

criteria.tech_led: QQQ is ahead of IWM by a top-third margin for this time of day and above its usual swing
criteria.small_led: IWM is ahead of QQQ by a top-third margin for this time of day and above its usual swing
criteria.both_ahead: both are in the top third of their own since the open for this time of day and their spread is not in the top third
criteria.both_behind: both are in the bottom third of their own and their spread is not in the top third
criteria.one_ahead_one_behind: one fund is in the top third of its own and the other in the bottom third, and their spread is not in the top third

code_criteria.tech_led: |spread| in the top third of the same since the settled open on the last {night_rank_count} sessions at this minute (rank >= {third_hi}), QQQ ahead, and QQQ's residual positive
code_criteria.small_led: |spread| top third, IWM ahead, and IWM's residual positive
code_criteria.both_ahead: |spread| below the top third; each residual (signed) in the top third of its own (rank >= {third_hi})
code_criteria.both_behind: |spread| below the top third; each residual in the bottom third (rank < {third_lo})
code_criteria.one_ahead_one_behind: |spread| below the top third; one residual in the top third of its own (rank >= {third_hi}) and the other in the bottom third (rank < {third_lo})

size_leadership_day.why: Leadership only shows over hours; the 30-minute version carries nothing and repeats move_breadth, so this is deliberately day-long. The label says who led and code learns the sign (textbook reads small-cap leadership as risk-on; this tape did the opposite).

groups.purpose: Outside markets ahead of the index (bonds, oil, the pooled macro complex, sector risk rotation) and the calendar (expiry cycle, month turn).

bond_catchup.ask: Are Treasuries ahead of the index, and which way?
bond_catchup.instructions: Read `xasset.bond_gap_30min`. Over the last {window_30_min} minutes, are Treasuries ahead of the index in the direction that has gone with stocks rising this hour, ahead in the stocks-falling direction, in line, or is the link too loose to say?

criteria.bonds_ahead_up: bonds moved further than the index's move would match, in the direction that has gone with stocks rising this hour, and the link is above the bottom third of recent sessions' at this time
criteria.bonds_ahead_down: bonds moved further than the index's move would match, in the direction that has gone with stocks falling, and the link is above the bottom third
criteria.in_line: bonds and the index moved by matching amounts under this hour's link
criteria.link_loose: bonds and stocks moved together this hour more loosely than on most recent sessions (the link's size in the bottom third), or the bond market is closed

code_criteria.bonds_ahead_up: gap rank >= {top_fifth} in the stocks-up direction and |link| ranked above the bottom third of the same hour's on the last {night_rank_count} sessions at this minute (rank >= {third_lo})
code_criteria.bonds_ahead_down: rank >= {top_fifth} stocks-down direction and |link| above the bottom third
code_criteria.in_line: middle three fifths and |link| above the bottom third
code_criteria.link_loose: |link| in the bottom third (rank < {third_lo}) or SIFMA holiday

bond_catchup.why: When Treasury prices run ahead of what the index's move would match and the two have been trading together, the index tends to follow; the label states today's link sign, so it works in either stock-bond regime. $TNX bars stop at 15:00, so TLT or /ZN is the source.

oil_gap.ask: Did oil move further than its usual link to the index explains?
oil_gap.instructions: Read `xasset.oil_gap_30min`. Over the last {window_30_min} minutes, did oil move further than its usual link to the index would explain, and which way?

criteria.oil_ran_up: oil rose more than the index's move usually brings, top fifth for this half hour
criteria.oil_ran_down: oil fell more than the index's move usually brings, bottom fifth
criteria.in_line: an ordinary amount given the index

oil_gap.why: Oil has moved against stocks in this tape; an oil jump the index has not absorbed has come before weakness. Code learns the sign; the label never says bullish or bearish.

macro_lean.ask: Are bonds, credit, oil, gold and the euro ahead of the index, and which way?
macro_lean.instructions: Read `xasset.macro_gap_30min` and `price.recent_move`. Taken together, are bonds, high-yield credit, oil, gold and the euro ahead of the index in the stocks-up direction, ahead in the stocks-down direction, or in line?
macro_lean.dark_reason: minute bars for euro futures (/6E), which the market-context job (market_context.SYMBOLS) does not fetch

criteria.complex_ahead_up: the outside markets together moved further toward stocks-up than the index did, top fifth
criteria.in_line: the outside markets and the index agree in size

macro_lean.why: One pooled read catches macro repricing the index has not joined yet, without near-duplicate single-asset questions. It replaces cross_asset_confirm, whose UUP feed is broken and whose risk-off signs are wrong in this tape, and absorbs gold.

risk_rotation.ask: Did risk-on sectors beat or trail the defensive ones?
risk_rotation.instructions: Read `leaders.rotation_30m`. After allowing for each sector's usual link to the index, did financials, discretionary and industrials beat utilities, staples and health care, trail them, or neither?

criteria.risk_on: the sensitive sectors beat the defensives by more than on most recent sessions at this time: the gap in the top third
criteria.risk_off: the defensives beat the sensitive sectors: the gap in the bottom third
criteria.level: the gap in the middle third

code_criteria.risk_on: sensitive-minus-defensive residual gap, signed, ranks in the top third of the same on the last {night_rank_count} sessions at this minute (rank >= {third_hi})

risk_rotation.why: Sector risk appetite beneath the index; unproven, live.

expiry_calendar.cadence: the 10:02 read and the 14:02 read, awake only on an expiry day or inside the opex-week or after-opex window
expiry_calendar.sleep_when: no quarter-end or monthly expiry today, and outside the opex-week window ({one_day} to {opex_week_days} trading days before the monthly) and the after-opex window ({one_day} to {after_opex_days} trading days after it)
expiry_calendar.ask: Which part of the expiry cycle is today?
expiry_calendar.instructions: Read `calendar.expiry_phase`. Check in order: quarter_end, monthly_or_quarterly, opex_week, week_after_opex. Which part of the expiry cycle is today?

criteria.quarter_end: the quarter's last trading day: the quarter-end SPXW book settles at today's close
criteria.monthly_or_quarterly: monthly or quarterly expiry: the morning-settled monthly book settled on the opening prints and daily SPXW settle at the close
criteria.opex_week: inside the opex-week window before this month's monthly expiry
criteria.week_after_opex: one of the trading days after a monthly expiry

expiry_calendar.why: SPX lists an expiry every day, but the monthly is morning-settled (its gamma is gone after Friday's open) while the quarter-end book is close-settled. Split out of calendar_flow_day so the one-window rule no longer hides 09-30.

month_turn_flow.cadence: the 10:02, 12:02, 14:32 and 15:32 reads, awake only in the month's first or last days
month_turn_flow.sleep_when: outside the month's first {month_turn_days} and last {rebal_window_days} trading days
month_turn_flow.ask: Which month-turn flow is in play for the rest of today?
month_turn_flow.instructions: Read `calendar.month_turn` and `flows.rebalance_side`. Which month-turn flow is in play for the rest of today?
month_turn_flow.dark_reason: the index's daily closes, which nothing saves, so the month-turn rebalance side (flows.rebalance_side) is never measured

criteria.last_days_stocks_overweight: one of the month's last sessions after stocks beat bonds by a top-fifth margin: funds expected to sell stocks, mostly into the close
criteria.last_days_stocks_underweight: one of the last sessions after stocks lagged bonds by a bottom-fifth margin: funds expected to buy stocks into the close
criteria.last_days_small_gap: one of the last sessions with an ordinary stock-bond gap
criteria.first_days_of_month: one of the first sessions of a new month, when new money is typically invested

code_criteria.last_days_stocks_overweight: trading days to month-end < {rebal_window_days} and the governing gap (named in the label) rank >= {top_fifth}

month_turn_flow.why: Turn of the month is the one calendar window with a local direction tilt; the rebalance side is worded as a close-and-next-day flow, which matches the published mechanism. It replaces calendar_flow_day's regime role and the sign lives in the options.

groups.purpose: The dark news feed seen through the tape: sudden bursts, whether they set extremes, the reaction path after any release or burst, vol's reaction, what moved with the shock, and single-name shocks.

shock_state.cadence: every 30-minute read and every 5-minute lane read
shock_state.sleep_when: no five-minute window in the last {shock_lookback_min} minutes larger than the biggest five-minute move of the {shock_lookback_min} minutes to its minute (from the settled open when that is shorter) on every one of up to the last {night_rank_count} sessions, or fewer than {same_clock_min_sessions} sessions to rank it
shock_state.ask: What has price done since the last hour's shock?
shock_state.instructions: Read `shock.burst`. Price had a sudden burst in the last hour: a five-minute move larger than the biggest five-minute move of the hour to that minute (from the settled open when that is shorter) on every one of the recent sessions. What has happened since? Check in order: fresh, round_trip, settling.

criteria.fresh: a burst passed the shock rule and ended within the fresh window
criteria.round_trip: a burst older than the fresh window, and price has since given back more than the half line of it
criteria.settling: a burst older than the fresh window, and price has kept the half line or more of it

shock_state.why: News with no feed shows up as a burst far bigger than the tape usually moves at that time of day; volatility clusters, so a fresh or round-tripped shock means a busier next half hour, even when the net move looks small. Every window is ranked against the biggest five-minute move of the same hour on recent sessions, so an hour of windows does not throw up a shock by chance.

shock_at_extreme.cadence: every 30-minute read, awake only within an hour of a shock
shock_at_extreme.ask: Where did the shock take price against today's range?
shock_at_extreme.instructions: Read `shock.burst` and `shock.vs_day_range`. Where did the last hour's shock take price against today's range so far?

criteria.new_extreme_now: the shock set a new session high or low and price is still at it: its distance back from the new extreme is in the bottom third of how far recent sessions sat from their own session extreme at this time
criteria.new_extreme_given_up: the shock set a new session high or low but price's distance back from it is in the middle or top third of recent sessions'
criteria.inside_range: the shock stayed inside the day's earlier high and low

code_criteria.new_extreme_now: burst passed the prior session extreme; |new extreme - spot| ranked against the last {night_rank_count} sessions' distance from their same-side session extreme at this minute: bottom third
code_criteria.new_extreme_given_up: passed it; middle or top third

shock_at_extreme.why: A burst that runs stops through the day's extreme with nothing behind it tends to snap back; a burst inside the range is more often real repricing. The side lives in the label.

move_reaction_path.cadence: every 30-minute read and lane read, awake 10-120 minutes after a release, Fed remarks, or a detected burst
move_reaction_path.sleep_when: the first reaction's move is in the bottom third of the same minutes' moves on the last {night_rank_count} sessions, event or not, or fewer than {same_clock_min_sessions} sessions to rank it
move_reaction_path.ask: What has price done since the first reaction to the latest release or burst?
move_reaction_path.instructions: Read `event.reaction`. What has price done since the first reaction to the latest release, Fed remarks or sudden burst? The label names which kind it was. Check extending first.

criteria.extending: price pushed past where the first reaction ended, the same way
criteria.holding: kept the half line or more of the first reaction without extending
criteria.faded: gave back more than the half line but has not crossed where the reaction started
criteria.reversed: crossed back through where the reaction started

code_criteria.faded: giveback > {gap_half_share}, same side of the start

move_reaction_path.why: Unscheduled headlines are SPX's largest move source and there is no feed, but the burst they leave is visible. Widening the trigger from the calendar to any burst lets the question fire about once a day and be graded; on Fed days the reaction starts at the press conference, where the real move came.

shock_vol_reaction.cadence: every 30-minute read, awake only within an hour of a shock
shock_vol_reaction.ask: Did VIX overreact or shrug at the shock?
shock_vol_reaction.instructions: Read `shock.burst` and `vol.vix_on_shock`. Since just before the shock, has VIX moved more than the price move alone explains, in line with it, or less, against the same minutes on the recent sessions? The label's third decides.

criteria.vol_overreacted: VIX's leftover beyond what the price move explains is in the top third of the recent sessions' over the same minutes

code_criteria.vol_overreacted: residual, ranked with VIX furthest above price highest against the same minutes on the prior sessions, shock or not: share of them it beats > {third_hi}

shock_vol_reaction.why: Whether options traders repriced risk is the best live proxy for 'was there a headline'; research expects repricing to mean drift, the station's small sample leans the other way, so the loop learns the sign.

shock_fingerprint.cadence: every 30-minute read, awake only within an hour of a shock
shock_fingerprint.instructions: Read `shock.burst` and `shock.cross_asset`. During the shock's five minutes, which group moved furthest beyond its usual link to the index, against the same five minutes on recent sessions? Pick the first the labels put in the top fifth.

criteria.rates_led: the ten-year yield's move beyond its link was in the top fifth of the same five minutes on recent sessions
criteria.tech_led: semiconductors' move beyond their link, the shock's way, was in the top fifth
criteria.one_name: one megacap supplied more than its share rule of the burst
criteria.broad: the count of sector funds moving the shock's way was in the top fifth and NYSE TICK reached its burst band for those minutes the same way
criteria.defensive_bid: utilities, staples and health care rose against a falling index, their move against it in the top fifth
criteria.no_fingerprint: nothing reached the top fifth: the shock was the index alone

code_criteria.rates_led: |dTNX residual| (bp) rank >= {top_fifth} against the same five minutes on the last {night_rank_count} sessions
code_criteria.tech_led: SMH residual in the shock's direction rank >= {top_fifth}
code_criteria.broad: count of sector funds with the shock rank >= {top_fifth} (ties not beaten) and a $TICK bar at or past its {tick_burst_pct} same-minute band the shock's way
code_criteria.defensive_bid: index falling and the defensive residual against it rank >= {top_fifth}

shock_fingerprint.why: With no headline feed, what moved with the shock says what kind of news it was (rates or Fed headline, AI or chip news, macro shock hitting everything, single-company news, flight to safety); each kind resolves differently.

single_name_shock.cadence: every 30-minute read and lane read, awake only when a top-8 name's 10-minute move beat every one of its own last 20 sessions at this minute
single_name_shock.sleep_when: no top-{mega_count} name's |{window_10_min}-minute move| higher than every one of its own last {night_rank_count} sessions at this minute; fewer than {same_clock_min_sessions} prior sessions with that name; no index weights on file
single_name_shock.ask: Did the big stock's shock stay alone or spread to other giants?
single_name_shock.instructions: Read `leaders.single_name_10m`. One of the largest index stocks just made a {window_10_min}-minute move larger than every one of its own recent sessions at this minute. Did it move alone, or did other giants join?
single_name_shock.dark_reason: the index weights of its largest stocks (state/spx_leaders/weights.json), which nothing writes yet

criteria.shock_up_alone: one heavy name jumped by more than every one of its recent sessions at this minute and fewer than {spread_count} other large names rose by a top-third move of their own
criteria.shock_down_alone: one heavy name dropped by more than every one of its recent sessions and fewer than {spread_count} others fell by a top-third move of their own
criteria.shock_up_spreading: one heavy name jumped by more than every one of its recent sessions and at least {spread_count} others rose by a top-third move of their own too
criteria.shock_down_spreading: one heavy name dropped by more than every one of its recent sessions and at least {spread_count} others fell by a top-third move of their own too

code_criteria.shock_up_alone: one name's |{window_10_min}-minute move| higher than every one of its own last {night_rank_count} sessions at this minute, up; fewer than {spread_count} others up in the top third of their own
code_criteria.shock_up_spreading: one name higher than every one, up; {spread_count}+ others up in the top third of their own

single_name_shock.why: Unscheduled single-name headlines (export rules, rulings, product news) move a stock before they move SPX; 'alone' is company news the index can digest, 'spreading' is a theme repricing.

groups.purpose: The 15:02 and 15:32 reads (from 14:02 for the settle pull): the afternoon leg the auction undoes, the settlement pull, the charm wall, late volume, and Fed press-conference afternoons.

afternoon_leg_into_close.horizon: 30min at the 15:32 read; 60min at the 15:02 read
afternoon_leg_into_close.cadence: the 15:02 and 15:32 reads only (weights keyed per read slot)
afternoon_leg_into_close.ask: Which way has price run since the early afternoon?
afternoon_leg_into_close.instructions: Read `price.afternoon_leg`. It sizes the move since the early-afternoon anchor against the same stretch on the recent sessions. Which way has price run since then?

criteria.afternoon_up: price has risen, a move in the middle or top third of the recent sessions' moves since 14:00 at this time of day
criteria.afternoon_down: price has fallen, a move in the middle or top third of them
criteria.afternoon_flat: the move since 14:00 is in the bottom third of them (no real move)

code_criteria.afternoon_up: anchor to now > 0 and |move| larger than a third or more of the last {night_rank_count} sessions' |move since 14:00| at this minute (middle or top third)
code_criteria.afternoon_flat: |move| larger than under a third of them (bottom third)

afternoon_leg_into_close.why: In the last half hour the closing auction undoes the afternoon's run; the 90-minute leg is the signal, not round 1's 30-minute leg or the day move. Earlier in the afternoon the same leg continues, so code learns a per-slot mapping. The day move from yesterday's close and the range position ride in the label (close_stretch merged: they add nothing once the leg is known).

settle_pull_side.cadence: the 14:02, 14:32, 15:02 and 15:32 reads (weights keyed per read slot: the pull shows only after 15:30)
settle_pull_side.sleep_when: magnet_seat's code answer is held_on_magnet or seated_fresh (the magnet's distance in the bottom third), or its rank has fewer than {same_clock_min_sessions} sessions
settle_pull_side.ask: Where does today's heaviest strike sit against price before the settle?
settle_pull_side.instructions: Read `gex.settle_pull`. Check split first. Where does today's heaviest same-day strike sit against price, counted in what today's options still price before the settle?

criteria.magnet_above_in_reach: the magnet is above price, its distance in remaining straddles in the bottom or middle third of recent sessions' at this time
criteria.magnet_above_out_of_reach: the magnet is above price, its distance in remaining straddles in the top third
criteria.magnet_below_in_reach: the magnet is below price, bottom or middle third
criteria.magnet_below_out_of_reach: the magnet is below price, top third
criteria.split: the magnet and the gamma-weighted centre sit on opposite sides of price

code_criteria.split: magnet and pin_centroid more than {settle_seat_sigma} on opposite sides of price (checked first)
code_criteria.magnet_above_in_reach: above, R ranked against the last {night_rank_count} sessions' at this minute below the top third

settle_pull_side.why: SPXW settles on the 16:00 print and dealer rehedging into settlement pulls the close toward the heavy strike, but locally only after 15:30 and through the 15:50 auction; the ruler for 'how far' shrinks all afternoon because today's options die at the close, so distance is counted in remaining straddles.

afternoon_charm_wall.ask: Where does the charm wall sit against price?
afternoon_charm_wall.instructions: Read `gex.charm_wall_distance`. Where does the charm wall sit compared with price?

criteria.charm_at_price: the charm wall's distance is in the bottom third of recent sessions' at this time
criteria.charm_above_near: above price, in the middle third
criteria.charm_below_near: below price, in the middle third

code_criteria.charm_at_price: |distance| ranked against the last {night_rank_count} sessions' at this minute: bottom third

afternoon_charm_wall.why: Unproven, not disproven, so live on a 30-minute horizon (what the evidence measured); the charm sign never varies (negative on 50/50 days), so only the location is asked, with remaining straddles in the label.

late_volume_pace.ask: How heavy was trading in the last {window_30_min} minutes for this time of day?
late_volume_pace.instructions: Read `volume.spy_last30_share`. How heavy was trading in the last {window_30_min} minutes, as a share of the day's volume, compared with the same minute on recent sessions?

criteria.heavy: the last half hour's share of the day's volume ranked in the top third for this minute on recent sessions
criteria.normal: that share ranked in the middle third
criteria.light: that share ranked in the bottom third

code_criteria.heavy: share higher than more than {third_hi} of the same share at this minute on up to the last {night_rank_count} sessions, needing {same_clock_min_sessions} (top third)

late_volume_pace.why: The closing auction is the day's biggest volume event; a heavy last half hour means programs are already working and the close moves further. It feeds P(flat) at the read where the clock baseline is weakest.

fed_presser_path.cadence: every 30-minute read after the press conference starts, FOMC days only (none in the test window; next 10-28)
fed_presser_path.ask: Since the Fed press conference began, has price extended or reversed the statement's move?
fed_presser_path.instructions: Read `event.statement_and_presser`. Check presser_flat, then presser_new_leg, then extends or reverses. Since the Fed chair's press conference began, has price gone with the statement's first move, against it, or nowhere, judged against the same minutes on recent sessions?

criteria.presser_extends: since the press conference began price moved the same way as the statement's move, and both moves are above the bottom third of the same minutes' moves on recent sessions
criteria.presser_reverses: the press conference moved price the other way, both moves above the bottom third
criteria.presser_new_leg: the statement's first move was in the bottom third of the same minutes on recent sessions and the press conference's move is not
criteria.presser_flat: the press conference's move is in the bottom third of the same minutes on recent sessions

code_criteria.presser_flat: |presser| (start to now) in the bottom third of the same minutes on the last {night_rank_count} sessions (checked first)
code_criteria.presser_new_leg: |statement| (its first reaction window) in the bottom third of the same minutes, |presser| not
code_criteria.presser_extends: same sign, neither in the bottom third
code_criteria.presser_reverses: opposite sign, neither in the bottom third

fed_presser_path.why: On both FOMC days on disk the real move came during the press conference and lasted to the close; the statement's 15 minutes said little.

closing_window_vix.cadence: the 15:02 and 15:32 reads (weights keyed per read slot)
closing_window_vix.ask: Has VIX drifted up, held or drifted down since the early afternoon?
closing_window_vix.instructions: Read `vol.vix_since_1400`. Since the early-afternoon anchor the label names, has VIX drifted up, held or drifted down, as a share of its level, against the same minutes on the recent sessions? The label's third decides.

criteria.vix_drifting_up: VIX's change since the anchor is in the top third of the recent sessions' over the same minutes (a rise, or a smaller fall than usual)
criteria.vix_drifting_down: in the bottom third (a fall, or a smaller rise than usual)

code_criteria.vix_drifting_up: change/VIX, ranked with a rise highest against the same on the prior sessions from the anchor to this minute: share of them it beats > {third_hi}

closing_window_vix.why: Hedges bought or unwound into the close move VIX before the closing auction moves SPX; the afternoon drift is the one VIX read keyed to the close.

groups.purpose: 30-minute lane: the day's move and breadth across the lane's last reads, rebuilt from bars at the earlier read minutes.

seq_day_move_stage.sleep_when: |day move from the settled open| ranks below {third_lo} against the same move at this minute on the last {night_rank_count} sessions (bottom third) or is not ranked (fewer than {same_clock_min_sessions} sessions), fewer than two earlier reads today, or fewer than {same_clock_min_sessions} sessions ranked at these read minutes
seq_day_move_stage.ref_side: the day's move from the settled open
seq_day_move_stage.ask: Across the lane's last reads, is the day's move from the open still making new ground, stalled, or unwinding?
seq_day_move_stage.instructions: Read `seq.day_move_by_read`. Where price is now against the settled open decides first; the stage words decide the answer.

criteria.extending: this read set the day's furthest point from the open so far
criteria.stalled: the furthest point came at an earlier read and the share of it given back is in the bottom or middle third for these reads on the recent sessions
criteria.unwinding: the furthest point came at an earlier read and the share of it given back is in the top third for these reads on the recent sessions

code_criteria.extending: furthest point from the settled open is at this read
code_criteria.stalled: furthest point earlier; giveback share rank at most {third_hi} vs the same read minutes over the last {night_rank_count} sessions
code_criteria.unwinding: furthest point earlier; giveback share rank above {third_hi}

seq_day_move_stage.why: A move that keeps making new ground read after read differs from one whose high came two reads ago; no single-window question says which read the extreme came at.

seq_breadth_drift.sleep_when: |day move from the settled open| ranks below {third_lo} against the same move at this minute on the last {night_rank_count} sessions (bottom third) or is not ranked (fewer than {same_clock_min_sessions} sessions), fewer than two earlier reads today, or fewer than {same_clock_min_sessions} sessions ranked at these read minutes
seq_breadth_drift.ref_side: the day's move from the settled open
seq_breadth_drift.ask: Across the lane's last reads, has breadth built behind the day's move, faded under it, or tracked it?
seq_breadth_drift.instructions: Read `seq.breadth_by_read`. Where price is now against the settled open decides first. Do not say which way price went. Check fading_under_move first.

criteria.fading_under_move: the volume share in rising stocks shifted away from the day's side more than usual while the move held or grew
criteria.building_behind_move: the share shifted toward the day's side more than usual
criteria.tracking: the share shifted about as usual

code_criteria.fading_under_move: change away from the day's side ranked above {third_hi} vs the same stretch over the last {night_rank_count} sessions, and the day move did not shrink below its value at the first listed read
code_criteria.building_behind_move: change toward the day's side ranked above {third_hi}

seq_breadth_drift.why: breadth_day_regime judges one moment; a divergence is a sequence: price keeps going while the volume behind it slips read after read.

groups.purpose: Micro bitcoin futures (/MBT) against the index in the session: the last half hour, three half hours in a row, how tightly they trade together today, and the last five sessions.

btc_gap_30m.sleep_when: excess rank in the middle three fifths; fewer than {same_clock_min_sessions} prior sessions at this clock; no bitcoin trade in the last {window_10_min} minutes
btc_gap_30m.ask: Did bitcoin run ahead of the index over the last half hour, and which way?
btc_gap_30m.instructions: Read `xasset.btc_gap_30min`. Over the last {window_30_min} minutes, did bitcoin move further than the index's move would match, in the direction that has gone with stocks rising, or in the direction that has gone with stocks falling?

criteria.btc_ahead_up: bitcoin moved further than the index's move would match, in the direction that has gone with stocks rising
criteria.btc_ahead_down: bitcoin moved further than the index's move would match, in the direction that has gone with stocks falling

code_criteria.btc_ahead_up: the excess ranks in the outer fifth on the side that has gone with stocks rising, against the same clock over the last {night_rank_count} sessions: >= {top_fifth} while bitcoin's usual multiple of the index is at or above zero, <= {bottom_fifth} while it is below
code_criteria.btc_ahead_down: the outer fifth on the side that has gone with stocks falling: <= {bottom_fifth} while the multiple is at or above zero, >= {top_fifth} while it is below

btc_gap_30m.why: The usual idea is that bitcoin is a fast risk gauge the index follows. Measured here, it runs the other way. When bitcoin has run ahead of the index in the last half hour, the index's next half hour leans slightly the opposite way. At the minute level the index leads bitcoin, not the reverse. The label reports the move and the link and does not say 'bitcoin leads', so the learning loop learns the sign.

btc_gap_streak.cadence: every 30-minute read from 11:02 (needs three prior half-hours)
btc_gap_streak.sleep_when: the three signs are mixed, or the summed excess is in the middle third; before 11:02; any of the three windows missing bitcoin data
btc_gap_streak.ask: Has bitcoin run ahead of the index the same way for three half-hours in a row?
btc_gap_streak.instructions: Read `xasset.btc_gap_streak`. Across the last three 30-minute reads, did bitcoin run ahead of the index in the same direction every time, toward stocks rising or toward stocks falling?

criteria.streak_up: three half-hours in a row bitcoin moved further than the index's move would match, each time in the direction that has gone with stocks rising
criteria.streak_down: three half-hours in a row bitcoin moved further than the index's move would match, each time in the stocks-falling direction

code_criteria.streak_up: the last three half-hour excesses all one sign, their sum ranking >= {third_hi} when all rose or <= {third_lo} when all fell, against the same clock over the last {night_rank_count} sessions, and that sign the side that has gone with stocks rising (rose while bitcoin's usual multiple of the index is at or above zero, fell while it is below)
code_criteria.streak_down: the same on the side that has gone with stocks falling (fell while the multiple is at or above zero, rose while it is below)

btc_gap_streak.why: One half-hour of bitcoin drift can be noise. Three in a row in the same direction is a steadier sign that risk appetite outside stocks is moving differently from the index. The measured effect is small and, like btc_gap_30m, runs against bitcoin's direction.

btc_link_today.sleep_when: link rank in the middle third; before 10:32 (too few minutes)
btc_link_today.ask: Are bitcoin and the index trading together today more tightly than usual, or less?
btc_link_today.instructions: Read `xasset.btc_link`. Since the open, have bitcoin and the index moved together five minutes by five minutes more tightly than on most of the last {night_rank_count} sessions, or more loosely?

criteria.tight: bitcoin and the index have moved together today more tightly than on most recent sessions
criteria.loose: bitcoin and the index have moved together today more loosely than on most recent sessions, or in opposite directions

code_criteria.tight: today's link rank vs the last {night_rank_count} sessions at this clock >= {third_hi}

btc_link_today.why: Bitcoin's tie to stocks comes and goes. Since 2020 the 60-session correlation of daily moves has run from -0.09 to 0.72. This year the 20-session figure fell from about 0.7 in March and April to 0.26 in August. A tight day says one risk mood is driving both markets. A loose day says bitcoin is on its own news, and its moves say little about stocks. This question tells the loop which days to trust the other bitcoin reads on.

btc_five_day_lead.cadence: once at the 09:35 read; answer held as a day constant through the 30-minute reads
btc_five_day_lead.sleep_when: rank in the middle three fifths; fewer than {same_clock_min_sessions} prior five-session stretches; a bitcoin roll inside the five sessions without a splice, or one pending
btc_five_day_lead.ask: Over the last week, has bitcoin been lagging the index or running ahead of it?
btc_five_day_lead.instructions: Read `xasset.btc_five_day`. Over the last five sessions, has bitcoin done worse than its usual tie to the index would match (lagging) or better (running ahead)?

criteria.btc_lagging: over the last five sessions bitcoin has done clearly worse than the index's move would match
criteria.btc_ahead: over the last five sessions bitcoin has done clearly better than the index's move would match

code_criteria.btc_lagging: five-session excess rank vs the last {night_rank_count} sessions <= {bottom_fifth}

btc_five_day_lead.why: The 'canary' idea is that bitcoin weakening while stocks hold up warns of a stock drop. The data does not support it. From 2020 to 2026, weeks when bitcoin lagged were followed by slightly better index days, not worse. The pattern was not stable in 2025-26. It is in the set because it is the most common bitcoin-for-stocks claim, and the loop should learn its sign rather than JEV assuming it.

groups.purpose: Pre-market lane, the 09:28 JEV read: the futures' move since their 16:00 price in the pre-open ruler, the night's range, which stretch of the night moved most unusually, and the night against yesterday's last cash hour; every checkpoint rebuilds the labels from the overnight store.

horizon.premarket: 10 and 30 minutes from the 09:34 settled open (the premarket lane's open_10 and open_30)

overnight_move_vs_expected.ask: Which way and how far have futures moved since their 16:00 price?
overnight_move_vs_expected.instructions: Read `overnight.es_move`. Where are S&P futures now against their 16:00 price, and how large is that move against the recent nights' moves to the same time?

criteria.big_down: futures are below their 16:00 price, a move in the top third of the recent nights' moves
criteria.down: below it, a move in the middle third of the recent nights' moves
criteria.flat: either side of it, a move in the bottom third of the recent nights' moves
criteria.up: above it, a move in the middle third of the recent nights' moves
criteria.big_up: above it, a move in the top third of the recent nights' moves

code_criteria.big_down: move < 0 and |move| in percent larger than over two thirds of the last {night_rank_count} usable nights' |move| to this minute (top third)
code_criteria.down: move < 0 and |move| larger than a third to two thirds of them (middle third)
code_criteria.flat: |move| larger than under a third of them (bottom third)
code_criteria.up: move > 0 and |move| larger than a third to two thirds of them (middle third)
code_criteria.big_up: move > 0 and |move| larger than over two thirds of them (top third)

overnight_move_vs_expected.why: A signed pre-open read of the overnight vote: it leans slightly against the move for the first half hour and with it from 10:30; code learns both signs by clock bucket.

horizon.premarket: 10 and 30 minutes from the 09:34 settled open (the premarket lane's open_10 and open_30)

pm_overnight_session.ask: How wide has the night's futures session been?
pm_overnight_session.instructions: Read `overnight.range_vs_normal`. How wide has the night's futures range been since the reopen, against the recent nights' ranges to the same time?

criteria.quiet_night: the night's range is in the bottom third of the recent nights' ranges

code_criteria.quiet_night: the range in percent of price is larger than under a third of the last {night_rank_count} usable nights' ranges to this minute (bottom third)
code_criteria.normal_night: larger than a third to two thirds of them (middle third)
code_criteria.wide_night: larger than over two thirds of them (top third)

pm_overnight_session.why: Volatility clusters overnight into the first hour, and futures pressing an edge at 09:28 set up an open outside the range: one read gives the 09:35 ten-minute call a size prior before any SPX bars exist.

horizon.premarket: 10 and 30 minutes from the 09:34 settled open (the premarket lane's open_10 and open_30)

gap_origin.sleep_when: the move since futures' 16:00 price ranks at or under {third_lo} against the last {night_rank_count} nights (no real gap), fewer than {overnight_rank_min_nights} usable nights, a roll night, a day the event calendar's releases before the open do not cover, or /ES bars missing
gap_origin.ask: Which stretch of the night moved most unusually for its time?
gap_origin.instructions: Read `overnight.gap_origin`. Where futures stand against their 16:00 price comes first. Which stretch of the night moved most unusually against the same stretch on the recent nights: early, in Europe, in the window after this morning's report, or late? On a morning with no report, the 08:30 to 08:45 stretch counts as late.

criteria.made_early: the most unusual stretch was after the close or in Asia
criteria.made_in_europe: the most unusual stretch was Europe's open or the Europe morning
criteria.made_at_release: the most unusual stretch was the window after this morning's early report, on a morning with a report
criteria.made_late: the most unusual stretch was the one before the report or the last one before the open, or on a morning with no report the 08:30 to 08:45 stretch

code_criteria.made_early: the stretch whose |move| ranks highest against the same stretch on the last {night_rank_count} nights is after_close or asia
code_criteria.made_at_release: it is report_window, on a day the calendar lists a report before the open
code_criteria.made_late: it is pre_report or last_stretch, or report_window on a day with no report

gap_origin.why: Where the night's move was made: in replay the part made early (after the close, Asia) reversed in the first hour, while the Europe leg carried on to the close (Asia leg against the first 60 minutes -0.23). Each stretch is ranked against its own usual, since as a share of the gap past a fixed half line the answer was 'overnight' on 81% of days.

horizon.premarket: 10 and 30 minutes from the 09:34 settled open (the premarket lane's open_10 and open_30)

night_vs_last_hour.sleep_when: |SPX's move in yesterday's last cash hour| rank <= {third_lo} over the last {night_rank_count} sessions, |net| rank <= {third_lo}, or data missing (too few prior sessions' last hours on file to rank)
