night_vs_last_hour.ask: Is the night carrying on yesterday's last cash hour, or turning against it?
night_vs_last_hour.instructions: Read `premarket.vs_last_hour`. Where futures are now decides first. Did the night go the way SPX moved in yesterday's last hour, or against it?

criteria.carried_on: the night went the same way as yesterday's last hour
criteria.turned_against: the night went against yesterday's last hour

code_criteria.carried_on: sign(net since futures' 16:00 price) == sign(SPX's move in yesterday's last cash hour)

night_vs_last_hour.why: Links two sessions in one sequence: late selling the night carries on differs from late selling the night reverses.

groups.purpose: Pre-market lane, 08:48 and 09:28 JEV reads: the early report's reaction path and the report window against the night, overnight Treasury futures against the S&P futures' move, and bitcoin's night and weekend against the S&P futures.

horizon.premarket: 10 and 30 minutes from the 09:34 settled open (the premarket lane's open_10 and open_30)

release_reaction_path.cadence: at the 09:28 premarket read on a day with a report before the open
release_reaction_path.sleep_when: no report before the open on the calendar today (a pre_open row after 08:00 and before 08:45; claims-only days are asked), fewer than {overnight_rank_min_nights} usable days, a roll inside the window, or /ES bars missing around it
release_reaction_path.ask: What did futures do after this morning's early report?
release_reaction_path.instructions: Read `overnight.release_reaction`. Where futures stand against their 16:00 price comes first. How large was the first reaction to this morning's early report against the same window on recent mornings, and what did futures do after it? Check in order: shrugged, extended, faded, held.

criteria.shrugged: the first reaction was in the bottom third of the same window's moves on recent mornings
criteria.extended: futures kept going the reaction's way by more than the half line of it
criteria.held: futures kept the half line or more of the reaction
criteria.faded: futures gave back more than the half line of the reaction

code_criteria.shrugged: |move from the release minute to the report window's end| larger than under a third of the same window's moves on the last {night_rank_count} days, report or not (bottom third)
code_criteria.extended: after the report window futures moved on the reaction's way by more than {gap_half_share} of it
code_criteria.held: given back at most {gap_half_share} of it
code_criteria.faded: given back more than {gap_half_share} of it

release_reaction_path.why: News at 08:30 is priced within a minute, so its direction is in the gap; what carries into the open is whether the market kept trading through it. The size of the reaction rides in the label for the size book.

horizon.premarket: 10 and 30 minutes from the 09:34 settled open (the premarket lane's open_10 and open_30)

overnight_bonds_vs_gap.sleep_when: fewer than {overnight_rank_min_nights} of the last nights with both futures measured on one contract, a roll between the two prices, bonds and S&P futures showing no link (leaving out a single night turns the fit's sign), or data missing
overnight_bonds_vs_gap.ask: Did Treasury futures move further overnight than the S&P futures' move would match?
overnight_bonds_vs_gap.instructions: Read `overnight.bond_gap`. Where Treasury futures stand against their 16:00 price comes first. Do they point S&P futures further toward stocks-up than where S&P futures stand, further toward stocks-down, or in line?

criteria.overnight_ahead_up: Treasury futures point S&P futures further toward stocks-up than where they stand
criteria.overnight_ahead_down: Treasury futures point S&P futures further toward stocks-down than where they stand
criteria.in_line: Treasury futures and S&P futures agree

code_criteria.overnight_ahead_up: where bonds point S&P futures (through the fit over the last {night_rank_count} nights) less where they stand ranks at or over {third_hi} (top third)

overnight_bonds_vs_gap.why: Overnight bonds reprice on news before cash stocks open; a gap that bonds did not match tends to trade back toward the bonds' side in the first hour. The sign and size of the link come from the last nights, never assumed. Bitcoin is its own question (btc_overnight_vs_futures).

horizon.premarket: 10 and 30 minutes from the 09:34 settled open (the premarket lane's open_10 and open_30)

release_vs_night.cadence: at the 08:48 and 09:28 premarket reads on a day with a report before the open
release_vs_night.sleep_when: no report before the open on the calendar today (claims-only days are asked), |reaction| rank <= {third_lo} vs the same window over the last {night_rank_count} days, |net at the release minute| rank <= {third_lo}, or data missing
release_vs_night.ref_side: the night's net move before the report
release_vs_night.ask: Did this morning's early report push the night's move further, undo part of it, or carry futures across their 16:00 price?
release_vs_night.instructions: Read `premarket.release_vs_night`. Where futures are now decides first. Compare the report window's move with the night's move before it. Check crossed_price first.

criteria.crossed_price: by the end of the report window futures had crossed their 16:00 price, to the other side from the night's move
criteria.unwound_night: the reaction went against the night's move without crossing the 16:00 price
criteria.extended_night: the reaction went the night's way

code_criteria.crossed_price: sign(net at the report window's end) != sign(net at the release minute)
code_criteria.unwound_night: sign(reaction) != sign(net at the release minute), no cross
code_criteria.extended_night: sign(reaction) == sign(net at the release minute)

release_vs_night.why: The sequence at the report itself: whether the news confirmed or overturned what the night had priced. release_reaction_path covers the reaction against its own aftermath; this covers it against the night before.

horizon.premarket: 10 and 30 minutes from the 09:34 settled open (the premarket lane's open_10 and open_30)

btc_overnight_vs_futures.sleep_when: excess rank in the middle three fifths; the Thursday bitcoin roll night or a roll pending; fewer than {overnight_rank_min_nights} clean prior nights; no /MBT trade in the last {window_10_min} minutes before the read
btc_overnight_vs_futures.ask: Did bitcoin move further overnight than S&P futures did, and which way?
btc_overnight_vs_futures.instructions: Read `overnight.btc_vs_futures`. Since the S&P futures' 16:00 price, or on the first session after a weekend or holiday since the futures reopened the evening before (bitcoin's weekend itself is a question of its own), did bitcoin move further than the futures' own move over the same span would match, in the direction that has gone with stocks rising, or in the direction that has gone with stocks falling?

criteria.btc_ahead_up: bitcoin went further than the futures' move would match, in the direction that has gone with stocks rising over the recent nights
criteria.btc_ahead_down: bitcoin went further than the futures' move would match, in the direction that has gone with stocks falling over the recent nights

code_criteria.btc_ahead_up: the gap to the futures ranks in the outer fifth on the side that has gone with stocks rising, against the last {night_rank_count} nights: >= {top_fifth} while bitcoin's usual multiple of the futures is at or above zero, <= {bottom_fifth} while it is below
code_criteria.btc_ahead_down: the outer fifth on the side that has gone with stocks falling: <= {bottom_fifth} while the multiple is at or above zero, >= {top_fifth} while it is below

btc_overnight_vs_futures.why: Bitcoin trades through the night and reacts to the same risk news as stocks. If it has moved further than futures, the thought is that stocks have not caught up yet. The data says futures already have: bitcoin's overnight move sits inside the gap (rank correlation +0.63 with the SPX open gap) and adds nothing after 09:30. It is here so the learning loop can confirm that, and because the owner asked for bitcoin in the pre-open read.

horizon.premarket: 10 and 30 minutes from the 09:34 settled open (the premarket lane's open_10 and open_30)

btc_weekend_path.cadence: at the 09:28 premarket read on the first session after a weekend or market holiday (the gate decides, never the schedule)
btc_weekend_path.sleep_when: weekend leg not in the top third by size of the last {night_rank_count} weekends (an ordinary weekend); not the first session after a weekend or holiday; fewer than {overnight_rank_min_nights} prior weekends; a bitcoin roll across either leg; no trade in the last {window_60_min} minutes of the weekend leg (the Saturday maintenance window)
btc_weekend_path.ref_side: sign of the weekend leg (the learning loop folds on it)
btc_weekend_path.ask: After a big bitcoin weekend, did bitcoin keep going, hold, or turn back once S&P futures reopened?
btc_weekend_path.instructions: Read `weekend.btc_path`. It gives bitcoin's weekend leg (from Friday's close until S&P futures reopened on Sunday evening) and its reopen leg (since the reopen). Taking the weekend leg's direction as the reference, did the reopen leg extend it, hold it, or turn back against it?

criteria.extended: after S&P futures reopened, bitcoin kept moving the same way as its weekend move
criteria.held: after the reopen bitcoin stayed about where the weekend left it
criteria.reversed: after the reopen bitcoin moved back against its weekend move

code_criteria.extended: reopen-leg rank vs the last {night_rank_count} reopen legs in the weekend leg's direction >= {third_hi}
code_criteria.held: reopen-leg rank in the middle third
code_criteria.reversed: reopen-leg rank against the weekend leg's direction >= {third_hi}

btc_weekend_path.why: Bitcoin is the one big market that trades all weekend, so it shows first how risk appetite moved while stocks were shut. A peer-reviewed study (Mourey, Shahrour, Soiman, Finance Research Letters 2025) finds that weak crypto weekends predict weaker Mondays for stocks and strong ones do not, an effect that grew after the May 2022 LUNA collapse. That study measures Friday close to Monday close, and at 09:28 the futures gap already contains most of it. This question asks the part the gap does not show: whether bitcoin's weekend verdict is being confirmed or taken back since futures reopened.

groups.purpose: Pre-market lane, 08:48 and 09:28 JEV reads: the night's story rebuilt from saved /ES bars at every read, four labels of at most 45 words each because every question in a group sees every label the group reads.

horizon.premarket: 10 and 30 minutes from the 09:34 settled open (the premarket lane's open_10 and open_30)

overnight_arc.sleep_when: no leg with |move| rank > {third_lo} (a quiet night), a roll night, or /ES bars missing
overnight_arc.ask: What has happened to the night's first real move since it was made?
overnight_arc.instructions: Read `premarket.where_now` and `premarket.arc`. Where futures are now against their 16:00 price decides first. Has the first leg that moved been built on, held, faded or reversed? Check in order: reversed, faded, built, held.

criteria.reversed: futures are now on the other side of their 16:00 price from the first move, by more than a quiet amount
criteria.faded: futures keep less than the half line of the first move
criteria.built: futures keep more than all of the first move: later trading pushed further the same way
criteria.held: futures keep between the half line and all of the first move

code_criteria.reversed: sign(net now) != sign(first moving leg) and |net now| rank > {third_lo} vs the same clock over the last {night_rank_count} nights

overnight_arc.why: Carries the night's sequence into a read with no memory: whether the first real move of the night was built on, held, faded or reversed is the shape a trader reads before the open.

horizon.premarket: 10 and 30 minutes from the 09:34 settled open (the premarket lane's open_10 and open_30)

latest_leg_vs_night.sleep_when: |leg| rank <= {third_lo} vs the same clock window over the last {night_rank_count} nights (a quiet leg), |net at previous checkpoint| rank <= {third_lo} (no direction to compare with), first checkpoint, or data missing
latest_leg_vs_night.ref_side: the night's net move before the leg
latest_leg_vs_night.ask: Since the previous checkpoint, did futures add to the night's move, give some back, or cross their 16:00 price?
latest_leg_vs_night.instructions: Read `premarket.where_now` and `premarket.since_checkpoint`. Where futures are now against their 16:00 price decides first. Check crossed first.

criteria.crossed: since the previous checkpoint futures crossed their 16:00 price, to the other side from the night's move
criteria.added: the latest leg went the night's way
criteria.gave_back: the latest leg went against the night's move without crossing the 16:00 price

code_criteria.crossed: sign(net now) != sign(net at the previous scheduled checkpoint)

latest_leg_vs_night.why: The 'what changed since the last read' question: it lets a read with no memory see the latest turn in the story.

horizon.premarket: 10 and 30 minutes from the 09:34 settled open (the premarket lane's open_10 and open_30)

night_legs_agree.sleep_when: fewer than two finished legs with rank > {third_lo}, |net| rank <= {third_lo}, or data missing
night_legs_agree.ask: Did every stretch of the night that moved push the same way, or did the latest one turn?
night_legs_agree.instructions: Read `premarket.where_now` and `premarket.legs`. Counting only the legs that moved, did they all go the night's way? Check one_way first.

criteria.one_way: every leg that moved went the night's way
criteria.latest_against: the latest leg that moved went against the night's move
criteria.split_latest_with: the legs split, and the latest leg that moved went the night's way

code_criteria.one_way: every leg with rank > {third_lo} has the net sign
code_criteria.latest_against: the latest leg with rank > {third_lo} has the opposite sign to net

night_legs_agree.why: Whether the world's sessions agreed is the plainest sequence summary: a night every region sold differs from one where Europe undid Asia. Covers 'is the direction consistent across reads'.

groups.purpose: Shadow only (proof they do not help): asked hourly, logged and graded, kept out of the weights.

flow_vs_price.shadow_proof: SPX aggressor tape, 20 and 46 days, worse than clock and shuffles
flow_vs_price.ask: Does the same-day options tape lean with the move or against it?
flow_vs_price.instructions: Read `price.recent_move` and `options.flow_lean_30`. Does the same-day options tape lean with the move, against it, or lean while price is still?

criteria.backs_move: price's 30-minute move ranked above the bottom third for this minute and the flow leaned the same way past its line
criteria.fights_move: price's 30-minute move ranked above the bottom third and the flow leaned the other way past its line
criteria.lean_while_still: price's 30-minute move in the bottom third for this minute while the flow leaned one way past its line
criteria.no_lean: the flow within its line of its usual level

code_criteria.backs_move: move rank {third_lo} or above, lean past {flow_lean_rank} rank the same way
code_criteria.fights_move: move rank {third_lo} or above, lean past {flow_lean_rank} rank the other way
code_criteria.lean_while_still: move rank below {third_lo}, lean past {flow_lean_rank} rank either way

flow_vs_price.why: Kept only as a log: the options aggressor lean on SPX's own tape has already been shown not to help.

option_quote_liquidity.shadow_proof: partial corr 0.005 after past movement, 21 days
option_quote_liquidity.ask: Are same-day option quotes near price thinner or deeper than usual?
option_quote_liquidity.instructions: Read `options.quote_liquidity`. Are same-day option quotes near price thinner or wider than usual for this time of day?

criteria.thin_or_wide: depth in the bottom fifth, or spread wider than its usual for this time; this comes first
criteria.normal: depth between the bottom and top fifths, and spread no wider than usual
criteria.deep: depth in the top fifth, and spread no wider than usual

code_criteria.thin_or_wide: depth rank <= {bottom_fifth}, or spread above usual (checked first)
code_criteria.normal: depth rank above {bottom_fifth} and below {top_fifth}, and spread not above usual
code_criteria.deep: depth rank >= {top_fifth}, and spread not above usual

option_quote_liquidity.why: Logged for completeness; measured, nothing there beyond past movement.

delta_weight_side.shadow_proof: residual -0.01 after spot; tracks price at -0.76
delta_weight_side.ask: Does dealers' directional exposure sit above or below price?
delta_weight_side.instructions: Read `gex.delta_weight_side`. The label's third words decide. Against the same share at this minute on recent sessions, does dealers' directional exposure hold more of itself at strikes above price than usual, more below, or about as usual? A top-third share can be under half: the thirds say more than usual, not which side holds most.

criteria.above: the share above price is in the top third of recent sessions' at this minute: more of it above price than usual
criteria.below: the share above price is in the bottom third: more of it below price than usual
criteria.even: the share above price is in the middle third: about as usual

code_criteria.above: dex_above_spot ranked against the last {night_rank_count} sessions' at this minute: top third

delta_weight_side.why: Built and unused by round 1; logged only, because it tracks where price sits in the day and adds nothing beyond price.

groups.purpose: Dark: the feed or data is missing on Monday; never asked. (Questions waiting only on a build stay dark in their home group.)

moc_imbalance_side.cadence: would need a 15:52 read with an 8-minute horizon (last live read is 15:32)
moc_imbalance_side.ask: Which side is the closing imbalance on, and is it large?
moc_imbalance_side.instructions: Read `close.moc_imbalance`. Which side is the published closing imbalance on, and is it large for today?
moc_imbalance_side.dark_reason: no closing-auction imbalance feed (a paid feed), and no read after 15:32 to use it

criteria.buy_large: a buy imbalance in the top fifth of recent closes
criteria.sell_large: a sell imbalance in the top fifth

moc_imbalance_side.why: 90% of the last 28 minutes' variance falls after 15:50, exactly the window this would see.

etf_flow_intraday.cadence: every 30-minute read when a feed exists
etf_flow_intraday.ask: Have index ETFs been created or redeemed heavily today?
etf_flow_intraday.instructions: Read `flows.etf_creations`. Since the open, have index ETFs been created or redeemed heavily for this time of day?
etf_flow_intraday.why: Intraday primary-market flow would show real money behind a move.

news_headline.cadence: on each new headline once a writer exists
news_headline.ask: What kind of market news just came out?
news_headline.instructions: Read `news.intraday_headline`. What kind of market news just came out, and is it new?
news_headline.dark_reason: no headline feed writes into state (a right-eye or Nexus writer is not built)

criteria.company_new: new single-company news in a large index stock
criteria.repeat: a repeat or rehash of known news

news_headline.why: Unscheduled headlines are SPX's largest move source; the price-only stand-ins are shock_state, shock_fingerprint and move_reaction_path.

nasdaq_breadth_lean.cadence: every 30-minute read when a feed exists
nasdaq_breadth_lean.ask: Did Nasdaq volume lean the same way as the NYSE?
nasdaq_breadth_lean.instructions: Read `breadth.nasdaq_net_volume`. Over the last half hour has Nasdaq volume leaned to rising or falling stocks, and does it agree with NYSE?
nasdaq_breadth_lean.dark_reason: no Nasdaq breadth series: Schwab serves no $TICKQ or $TRINQ history, $ADDQ is not a symbol, $VOLQ is stale, and $UVOLQ and $DVOLQ are not probed

criteria.nasdaq_leads_up: Nasdaq up-volume share in the top third of the same share at this minute on recent sessions while NYSE's is not
criteria.nasdaq_leads_down: Nasdaq share in the bottom third while NYSE's is not

code_criteria.nasdaq_leads_up: rank(share_q) top third, rank(NYSE) not top third, each ranked against the same measure at this minute on up to the last {night_rank_count} sessions (at least {same_clock_min_sessions}, else the label is omitted and the question skipped)
code_criteria.nasdaq_leads_down: rank(share_q) bottom third, rank(NYSE) not bottom third

nasdaq_breadth_lean.why: Kept so the gap stays visible: $VOLSPD is S&P 500 breadth, not Nasdaq.

spy_book_lean.cadence: every 5-minute lane read and 30-minute read once persisted
spy_book_lean.ask: Has the pressure at SPY's best prices been on the buy or the sell side?
spy_book_lean.instructions: Read `liquidity.spy_book_lean`. Over the last five minutes, has the pressure at SPY's best prices been on the buy side, the sell side, or balanced?
spy_book_lean.dark_reason: the lob-flow collector saves no per-minute SPY bid and ask sizes or order-flow imbalance

criteria.buyers_pressing: order-flow imbalance at least the lean line above usual
criteria.sellers_pressing: at least the lean line below usual

spy_book_lean.why: Top-of-book order-flow imbalance is the best-documented short-horizon price driver; most likely to help the 10-minute call.

tomorrow_book_handoff.cadence: the 15:02 and 15:32 reads once a 1DTE slice is scanned
tomorrow_book_handoff.ask: Where does tomorrow's heaviest strike sit as today's options run out?
tomorrow_book_handoff.instructions: Read `expiry.next_book_magnet`. Check next_priced_big first. As today's options run out, where does tomorrow's heaviest strike sit, and is tomorrow priced as a normal day?
tomorrow_book_handoff.dark_reason: the SPX scan writes no 1DTE slice, so tomorrow's book is not on the row

criteria.next_above_normal: tomorrow's heaviest strike is above price, its distance above the bottom third of recent sessions' at this time, usual pricing
criteria.next_below_normal: below price, its distance above the bottom third, usual pricing
criteria.next_at_price: its distance in the bottom third of recent sessions' at this time, usual pricing
criteria.next_priced_big: tomorrow's straddle in the top fifth of recent sessions at this clock

code_criteria.next_above_normal: next magnet above spot, |distance| rank against the last {night_rank_count} sessions above the bottom third, rank < {top_fifth}
code_criteria.next_below_normal: below, above the bottom third, rank < {top_fifth}

tomorrow_book_handoff.why: Tests the 0DTE-to-1DTE hand-off, which SNDK never had.

quarter_end_collar_side.cadence: every 30-minute read on the quarter's last trading day (09-30, 12-31) once the band is kept
quarter_end_collar_side.ask: Where is price against today's largest quarter-end strikes?
quarter_end_collar_side.instructions: Read `expiry.quarter_end_strikes`. Where does price sit against the largest strikes of the quarter-end options expiring today?
quarter_end_collar_side.dark_reason: the dated-book pull drops the expiring quarter-end band, so its strikes are not on the row

criteria.near_short_call: within the collar distance below the largest call strike
criteria.near_long_put: within the collar distance above the largest put strike

quarter_end_collar_side.why: The largest single SPX options position (the hedged-equity collar) rolls on the quarter's last day; the station cannot see that book on its own today.
